body.text: oṃ namo bhagavate mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince.

body.text: śaṅkhakṣīrendukundasphaṭikahimadalakṣaumaśubhrābhragauraiś cañcatspaṣṭāṭṭahāsair gaganatalagataiś chattrapaṅkty [ātapatraiḥ] stavyair bhūr bhāti yasya tridaśanaragarutsiddhagandharvājuṣṭaiḥ prahvās taṃ sarva eva praṇamata satataṃ buddham ādityabandhum.
body.translated_text: Radiant white as conch, milk, moon, jasmine, crystal, snowflake, linen, and bright clouds, with resplendent peals of loud laughter reaching the vault of heaven, with rows of parasols, praised by <s>tridaśa</s> (gods), men, <s>Garuḍa</s>s, <s>Siddha</s>s, and <s>Gandharva</s>s — all bow reverently and constantly pay homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, kinsman of the Sun.

body.text:
divyaiś candanacūrṇamiśranikarair mandānilodbhāsitair
vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgadundubhiravair gandharvagītisvaraiḥ
yo jātaḥ kṣitipālakaḥ pracalayan kṛtsnaṃ trilokālayaṃ
sarvajñāya niruddhasarvagataye buddhāya tasmai namaḥ.
body.translated_text: With divine sandalwood powder mixed in heaps, wafted by gentle breezes, with the sounds of <s>vīṇā</s>s, flutes, <s>mṛdaṅga</s>s, and <s>dundubhi</s> drums, with the melodious singing of <s>Gandharva</s>s — to him who was born as protector of the earth, shaking the entire triple world, to the Omniscient One whose every path is stilled, to that <s>Buddha</s>, homage!

body.text: bhagavatā sūtraṃ bhāṣitam.
body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> was spoken by the Blessed One.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma. jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat. sāvadānaṃ śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍopacaraṇam. yena śukasya māṇavasya taudeyaputrasya
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta</s>'s Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. He went carefully through <s>Śrāvastī</s> collecting alms-food. He approached the dwelling of the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s>.

body.text: niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. tena khalu punaḥ samayena śukasya māṇavasya taudeyaputrasya niveśane śaṅkhakuñjaro gonikāstṛte paryaṅke niṣaṇṇaḥ. aśmantakopadhānāyāṃ kāṃsyapātryāṃ śālimāṃsodanaṃ bhuṅkte. bhagavān adrākṣīt śaṅkhakuñjaraṃ goṇikāstṛte paryaṅke niṣaṇṇam aśmantakopādhānāyāṃ kāṃsyapātryāṃ paribhuñjānam. adrākṣīt śaṅkhakuñjaro bhagavantaṃ dvāramūle gatvā ca punar bukkati. atha bhagavān śaṅkhakuñjaram etad avocat. etad api te śaṅkha [cittaṃ] na damayati yad asi bhokārād bukkāram āgataḥ. evam ukte śaṅkhakuñjaro 'tiśayitaroṣaś caṇḍībhūto 'nāttamanā goṇikāstṛtāt paryaṅkād avatīryādhastāt paryaṅkasya dārusyandanikāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ. tena khalu punaḥ samayena śuko māṇavas
body.translated_text: He went to that dwelling. Now at that time, in the dwelling of the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s>, the dog <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> was seated on a couch spread with a woolen blanket, eating rice with meat from a bronze bowl on a stone pillow-rest. The Blessed One saw <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> seated on the couch spread with a woolen blanket, eating from a bronze bowl on the stone pillow-rest. <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> saw the Blessed One, went to the doorway, and barked. Then the Blessed One said this to <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>: 'Even this does not tame your mind, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, that you have come from eating to barking.' Thus addressed, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, exceedingly angered, fierce, and displeased, descended from the couch spread with the woolen blanket and sat beneath the couch on the wooden plank. Now at that time the young man <s>Śuka</s>

body.text: taudeyaputro bahir gato 'bhūt kenacid eva karaṇīyena. athāgacchac chuko māṇavas taudeyaputraḥ. adrākṣīt śuko māṇavas taudeyaputraś
body.translated_text: <s>Taudeyaputra</s> had gone out on some errand. Then the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> returned. The young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> saw

body.text: śaṅkhakuñjaram adhastād dārusyandanikāyāṃ prapatitam. dṛṣṭvā ḥ janam āmantrayate. kena vo yuṣmākaṃ śaṇkhakuñjaraḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> fallen down beneath the wooden plank. Having seen this, he addressed the people: 'Who among you has said something to <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>?'

body.text: kiṃcid uktaḥ. ko 'smākaṃ madhye madīyaputraṃ śaṅkhakuñjaraṃ kiṃcid vakṣyati. api tv āgato 'bhūt śramaṇo gautamaḥ. dvāramūle
body.translated_text: 'Who among us would say anything to my son <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>? But the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> came. Standing at the doorway,

body.text: 'vasthitaṃ tam itthaṃ bukkati. tam enaṃ śramaṇo gautama evam āha. etad api te śaṅkha na damayati yad asi bhokārād bukkāram āgataḥ. evam ukte śaṇkhakuñjaro 'tiśayitakupitaś caṇḍībhūto 'nāttamanā goṇikāstṛtāt paryaṅkād avatīryādhastāt paryaṅkasya dārusyandanikāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ. atha śukaḥ (kro)dhābhiṣaktaḥ kupitas caṇḍībhūto 'nāttamanā goṇikān niṣkramya yena jetavanam anāthapiṇḍadasyārāmas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān anekaśatāyāṃ bhikṣuparṣadi purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati. adrākṣīd bhagavān śukaṃ māṇavakaṃ taudeyaputraṃ dūrād evāgacchantam. dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma. paśyata yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śukaṃ māṇavaṃ taudeyaputram ita evāgacchantam. evaṃ bhadanta. sacec chuko māṇavas taudeyaputro 'smin samaye kālaṃ kuryāt. yathā bhallo nikṣiptaḥ evaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇād apāyadurgativinipāte 'vicau narakeṣūpapadyeta. tathā hy anena mamāntike cittaṃ pradūṣitam. cittapradūṣanād dhetor evam iha [ke] satvāḥ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇād apāyadurgatyavīcau narakeṣūpapadyante. athānyatamo bhikṣus tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate sma.
body.translated_text: the dog barked at him. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> said to him thus: "Even this does not tame you, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, that you have come from eating to barking." Thus addressed, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, exceedingly angered, fierce, and displeased, descended from the couch spread with the woolen blanket and sat beneath the couch on the wooden plank.' Then <s>Śuka</s>, seized by anger, furious, fierce, and displeased, went out from the dwelling and approached <s>Jeta</s>'s Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Now at that time, the Blessed One was seated before an assembly of many hundreds of monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One saw the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> coming from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'Look, monks, at the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> coming this way. So be it, venerable sir. If the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> were to die at this moment, just as a thrown javelin, so upon the breaking up of the body after death, he would be reborn in the miserable states, the evil destinies, the downfall, in the <s>Avīci</s> hell. For he has corrupted his mind against me. Because of corrupting the mind, beings here, upon the breaking up of the body after death, are reborn in miserable states, evil destinies, in <s>Avīci</s> hell.' Then a certain monk, at that moment, spoke this verse:

body.text:
praduṣṭacittaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva ekatyam iha pudgalam
etam arthaṃ vyākārṣīc chāstā bhikṣugaṇāntike.
idānīṃ batāvikṣepaṃ kālaṃ kurvīta māṇavaḥ
narakeṣūpapadyeta cittaṃ hy etena dūṣitam.
yathā hy ucitaṃ nikṣiptam evam eva tathāgate
cittapradūṣaṇād dhetoḥ satvā gacchanti durgatim.
body.translated_text: Having seen a certain person here with a corrupted mind, the Teacher declared this matter before the assembly of monks: 'If now the young man were to die without delay, he would be reborn in hell, for his mind has been corrupted. Just as a javelin thrown — even so toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> — because of corrupting the mind, beings go to evil destinies.'

body.text: adhikṣepya māṇavas taudeyaputro yena bhagavān tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ.
body.translated_text: Having reviled him, the young man <s>Taudeyaputra</s> approached the Blessed One.

body.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ sukhasaṃbhāvanāyāṃ saṃrajanīyāṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ śuko māṇavas taudeyaputro bhagavantam idam evāvocat. āgato bhagavān gautamo 'smākaṃ niveśanam. āgamane bhagavatā gautamena śaṅkhakuñjaraḥ kiṃcid uktaḥ. ihāhaṃ māṇava pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat. sāvadānaṃ śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍopacaraṇam. yena bhavato 'tra niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. upasaṃkramya dvāramūle 'vasthitaḥ. tena khalu punaḥ samayena śaṅkhakuñjaro goṇikāstṛtamañcake 'dhirūḍho 'śmantakopadhānāyāṃ kāṃsyapātryāṃ śālimāṃsodanaṃ paribhuṅkte. adrākṣīt śaṅkhakuñjaro māṃ dvāramūle 'vasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar bukkati. tam enam evaṃ vadā[mi. etad api te] śaṅkha na damayati yad asi bhokārād bukkāram āgataḥ. evam ukte śaṅkhakuñjaro 'bhiṣaktaḥ kupitaś caṇḍībhūto 'nāttamanā goṇikāstṛtāt paryaṅkād avatīryādhastāt paryaṅkasya dārusyandanikāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ. kiṃ punar bhagavān gautamaḥ śaṅkhakuñjarasyāsmākaṃ pūrvasyāṃ jātaṃ jānīte. alaṃ māṇava tiṣṭha mā etam arthaṃ pariprākṣīt. mā te bhaviṣyati āghātaś cākṣāntiś ca cetaso daurmanasyam. dvir api trir api śuko māṇavas taudeyaputro bhagavantam etad avocat. kiṃ punar bhagavān gautamo 'smākaṃ śaṅkhakuñjaraṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaṃ saṃjānīte. alaṃ māṇava tiṣṭha mā mām etam arthaṃ pariprākṣīt. mā ihaiva ca te bhaviṣyaty āghātaś cākṣāntiś ca cetaso daurmanasyam. anātha tvaṃ māṇava yāvad dvir api trir apy eta marthaṃ nā ...... māṇava śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru. bhāṣiṣye. yas te māṇava pitā taudeyaḥ sa eṣa kāyasya bhedād dhīnāyāṃ śvayonāv upapannaḥ. tad bho gautama evaṃ bhaviṣyati. asmākaṃ pitā ya iṣṭayajña āhitāgnir ucchritayūpaḥ sannīyate kāyasya bhedāt śubhre brahmaloke upapanno bhaviṣyaty. anenaiva te māṇava mānābhimānena pitā taudeyo mahādānapatiḥ śvayonāv upapannaḥ. pitur māṇava yadi me bhāṣitaṃ na
body.translated_text: Having approached, he exchanged pleasant and courteous words of various kinds with the Blessed One, and then sat down to one side. The young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'The Blessed <s>Gautama</s> came to our dwelling. Upon arrival, the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> said something to <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>.' 'Here, young man, I dressed in the morning, took my bowl and robe, and entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. I went carefully through <s>Śrāvastī</s> collecting alms-food. I approached your dwelling. Having approached, I stood at the doorway. Now at that time, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> had climbed onto the couch spread with a woolen blanket and was eating rice with meat from a bronze bowl on the stone pillow-rest. <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> saw me standing at the doorway, and upon seeing me, barked. I said to him thus: "Even this does not tame you, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, that you have come from eating to barking." Thus addressed, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, angered, furious, fierce, and displeased, descended from the couch spread with the woolen blanket and sat beneath the couch on the wooden plank.' 'Does the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> then know <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>'s former birth?' 'Enough, young man, stop. Do not ask me about this matter. Lest there be for you anger, impatience, and mental distress.' A second and third time the young man <s>Śuka</s> <s>Taudeyaputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Does the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> know our <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>'s former birth?' 'Enough, young man, stop. Do not ask me about this matter. Lest right here there be for you anger, impatience, and mental distress.' 'You are helpless, young man, since even a second and third time you ask about this matter... Young man, listen well and pay close attention. I shall speak. Your father, young man, <s>Taudeya</s>, upon the breaking up of the body, was reborn in a lowly dog birth. That is this very one.' 'O <s>Gautama</s>, how can this be so? Our father, who performed sacrifices, maintained the sacred fires, and erected sacrificial posts — it is established that upon the breaking up of the body he would have been reborn in the bright <s>Brahma</s>-world.' 'It is precisely because of this pride and conceit, young man, that your father <s>Taudeya</s>, the great patron, was reborn in a dog birth.' 'If you do not believe what I have said about your father, young man, then go to your dwelling.

body.text: śraddadhāsi tena hi tvaṃ māṇava yena te niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrama. upasaṃkramya śaṅkhakuñjaram evaṃ vada. saced bhavāñ chaṅkhakuñjaro 'smākaṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaḥ pitābhūt taudeyo 'dhiroha goṇikāstṛtaṃ paryaṅkam. adhirokṣyati. adhirūḍhaṃ caivaṃ vada. saced bhavāñ chaṅkhakuñjaro 'smākaṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaḥ pitābhūt taudeyaḥ paribhuñjīta bhavān. aśmantakopadhānāyāṃ kāṃsyapātryāṃ śālimāṃsodanaṃ paribhokṣyate. bhuktavantam enaṃ vada. saced bhavāñ chaṅkhakuñjaro 'smākaṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaḥ pitābhūt taudeyaḥ yat te 'smākaṃ maraṇasamaye mama santaṃ svāpateyaṃ nopadarśitaṃ tad upadarśaya. upadarśayiṣyati.
body.translated_text: Approach <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s> and say thus: "If you, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, were in a former birth our father <s>Taudeya</s>, then climb up onto the couch spread with the woolen blanket." He will climb up. And when he has climbed up, say thus: "If you, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, were in a former birth our father <s>Taudeya</s>, then eat the rice with meat from the bronze bowl on the stone pillow-rest." He will eat. When he has eaten, say to him: "If you, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, were in a former birth our father <s>Taudeya</s>, the personal wealth that was mine which you did not reveal to us at the time of your death — reveal it now." He will reveal it.'

body.text:
atha śuko māṇavas taudeyaputro bhagavatā bhāṣitam udgṛhya paryavāpya yena svakaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. upasaṃkramya śaṅkhakuñjaram etad avocat. saced bhavāñ chaṅkhakuñjaro 'smākaṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaḥ pitābhūt taudeyaḥ adhiroha. goṇikāstṛtaparyaṅke 'dhirūḍhaṃ cainam evam āha. saced bhavāñ chaṅkhakuñjaro 'smākaṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaḥ pitābhūt taudeyaḥ paribhuñjīta bhavān aśmantakopadhānāyāṃ kāṃsyapātryāṃ śālimāṃsodanam. paribhuktavān. bhuktavantaṃ cainam evam āha. saced bhavāñ chaṅkhakuñjaro 'smākaṃ pūrvikāyāṃ jātaḥ pitābhūt taudeyaḥ yat te 'smākaṃ maraṇasamaye mama santaṃ svāpateyaṃ nopadarśitaṃ tad upadarśaya. atha śaṅkhakuñjaro goṇikāstṛtaparyaṅkād avatīrya yenānyatamapurāṇavāsagṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. upasaṃkramya caturaḥ paryaṅkapādukān pādanakharikābhir avalikhitamadhyaṃ ca mukhatuṇḍakenopajighrati. yataḥ sa śuko māṇavas taudeyaputraḥ kṛtākṛtasya hiraṇyasuvarṇasya caturo lohasaṃghāṭān adhigatavān madhyāc ca sauvarṇakamaṇḍalum.
atha śuko māṇavas taudeyaputras tat suvarṇaṃ gopayitvā hṛṣṭatuṣṭodagraprītisaumanasyajātaḥ śrāvastyā niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān anekaśatāyāṃ bhikṣuparṣadi purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati. adrākṣīd
body.translated_text:
(MKV 28) Then <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, having learned and mastered what the Blessed One had spoken, approached his own dwelling. Having approached, he said this to <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>: 'If you, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, were born in our family and were our father <s>Taudeya</s>, climb up.' When he had climbed upon a couch spread with a woolen blanket, he said this to him: 'If you, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, were born in our family and were our father <s>Taudeya</s>, may you eat rice with meat from a bronze dish on a stone pillow.' He ate. And when he had eaten, he said this to him: 'If you, <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, were born in our family and were our father <s>Taudeya</s>, that which was your property at the time of death and which you did not show to me — show that.' Then <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>, descending from the couch spread with the woolen blanket, approached a certain old storehouse. Having approached, he scratched the middle of the four couch-legs with his toenails and sniffed with the tip of his snout. Whereupon <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, obtained four caskets of wrought and unwrought gold and silver, and from the middle a golden water-pot.
Then <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, having concealed that gold, joyful, pleased, elated, and filled with delight and gladness, departed from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and approached the Blessed One. At that time, the Blessed One was seated before an assembly of many hundreds of monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. He saw —

body.text: bhagavāñ chukaṃ māṇavaṃ taudeyaputraṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma. paśyatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śukaṃ māṇavaṃ taudeyaputraṃ dūrata evāgacchantam. evaṃ bhadanta. sacec chuko māṇavas taudeyaputro 'smin samaye kālaṃ kuryād yathā bhallo nikṣiptaḥ evaṃ kāyasya bhedāt sugatau svargalokeṣūpapadyeta. tathā hy anena mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditam. cittaprasādanahetor bhikṣavaḥ evam ihaike satvā kāyasya bhedāt sugatau svargalokeṣūpapadyante. athānyatamo bhikṣus tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate.
body.translated_text: — the Blessed One saw <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, coming from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'Do you see, monks, <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, coming from afar?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'If <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, were to die at this moment — just as an arrow once released — at the breaking up of the body, he would be reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly worlds. For he has generated faith in my presence. Due to the generation of faith, monks, thus some beings here, at the breaking up of the body, are reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly worlds.' Then a certain monk, at that occasion, spoke a verse:

body.text:
prasannacittaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva ekatyam iha pudgalam
etam arthaṃ vyākārṣīc chāstā bhikṣugaṇāntike.
idānīṃ gatadoṣo 'yaṃ kālaṃ kurvīta mānavaḥ
upapadyeta deveṣu cittam asya prasāditam.

body.translated_text:
'Having seen one person here with a clear mind,
the Teacher proclaimed this matter before the assembly of monks:
"If now this young man, freed from faults, were to die,
he would be reborn among the gods — his mind has been made clear.
Just as an arrow is released, even so toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
through the cause of generating faith, beings go to a good destination."'

body.text: atha śuko māṇavas taudeyaputro yena bhagavān tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ. evaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ śukaṃ māṇavaṃ taudeyaputraṃ bhagavān idam avocat. kaccin māṇava tathaiva yathā mayā śaṅkhakuñjaro vyākṛtaḥ. bho gautama tat tathaiva yathā bhagavatā gautamena śaṅkhakunjaro vyākṛtaḥ. anyad api tāvad vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ gautamaṃ pṛcchema kaṃcid eva pradeśaṃ saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnavyākaraṇāya. pṛccha māṇava yady evaṃ kāṅkṣasi. ko bho gautama hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ yenehaike satvā alpāyuṣo 'pi dīrghāyuṣo 'pi bahvābādhā api alpābādhā api durvarṇā api suvarṇā api alpeśākhyā api maheśākhyā api nīcakulīnā api uccakulīnā api anādeyavākyā api ādeyavākyā api alpabhogā api mahābhogā api duṣprajñā api mahāprajñā api. kasya nu bho gautama karmaṇo vipākenedaṃ satvānāṃ nānātvaṃ prajnāyate.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged various pleasant and agreeable words face to face with the Blessed One and sat down at one side. When <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, had thus sat down, the Blessed One said this to him: 'Was it, young man, just as I had declared concerning <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>?' 'Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, it was indeed just as the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> had declared concerning <s>Śaṅkhakuñjara</s>.' 'Furthermore, we would ask the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> about a certain topic, if he would grant us the opportunity for asking and answering questions.' 'Ask, young man, if you so wish.' 'What, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, is the cause, what is the condition, by which some beings here are short-lived and some long-lived, some much-afflicted and some little-afflicted, some ugly and some beautiful, some of little influence and some of great influence, some low-born and some high-born, some whose words carry no weight and some whose words carry weight, some of little wealth and some of great wealth, some of poor wisdom and some of great wisdom? By the ripening of what action, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, is this diversity among beings known?'

body.text: tatra bhagavāñ chukaṃ māṇavakaṃ taudeyaputram idam avocat. karmavibhaṅgaṃ te māṇavaka dharmaparyāyaṃ deśayiṣyami. tenahi
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said this to <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>: 'I shall teach you, young man, the <s>Dharma</s> discourse on the classification of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmavibhaṅga</s>). Therefore —'

body.translated_text: '— listen well and attend carefully. I shall speak.' 'Yes, Blessed One,' <s>Śuka</s>, the young brahmin student, son of <s>Taudeya</s>, replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: 'I declare, young man, that beings are owners of their <s>karma</s>, heirs to their <s>karma</s>, born from their <s>karma</s>, have their <s>karma</s> as their refuge. <s>Karma</s>, young man, divides beings — that is, into states of inferiority, superiority, and middlingness. As follows: there is <s>karma</s> tending toward short life; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward long life; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward many illnesses; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward few illnesses; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward ugliness; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward a pleasant appearance; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward little influence; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward great influence; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward birth in a low family; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward birth in a high family; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward little wealth; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward great wealth; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward poor wisdom; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward great wisdom; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the hells; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the animal realm; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the realm of hungry ghosts; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the realm of <s>Asuras</s>; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the human world; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the desire realm; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the form realm; there is <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the formless realm; there is <s>karma</s> that is done but not accumulated; there is <s>karma</s> that is accumulated but not done; there is <s>karma</s> that is both done and accumulated; there is <s>karma</s> that is neither done nor accumulated; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the hells, having exhausted the full lifespan of a hell-being, passes away; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the hells, having exhausted half the lifespan of a hell-being, passes away; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, just upon being reborn in the hells, immediately passes away; there is <s>karma</s> of determined rebirth; there is <s>karma</s> of undetermined rebirth; there is <s>karma</s> ripening in another region; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, having first been happy, afterward becomes unhappy; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, having first been unhappy, afterward becomes happy; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, having first been happy, afterward remains happy; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, having first been unhappy, afterward remains unhappy; there is <s>karma</s> —'

body.translated_text: '— by which a person becomes wealthy but miserly; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes poor but generous; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes wealthy and generous; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person [becomes poor and miserly]. There is a person whose <s>karma</s> is exhausted but not his lifespan; there is a person whose lifespan is exhausted but not his <s>karma</s>; there is a person whose both lifespan and <s>karma</s> are exhausted; there is a person whose lifespan is exhausted and whose merit is also exhausted; there is a person whose lifespan is not exhausted and whose <s>karma</s> is not exhausted, but whose <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are exhausted; there is a person who is happy in body but not in mind; there is a person who is happy in mind but not in body; there is a person who is happy both in body and mind; there is a person who is happy neither in body nor in mind; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the lower realms, is beautiful, with a smooth body, smooth complexion, pleasing to the eye, and handsome; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the lower realms, is ugly, with a rough body, terrible to behold, and repulsive in appearance; there is <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the lower realms, is foul-smelling, with crooked faculties and indistinct faculties. By the ripening of the ten unwholesome courses of action, the increase of ten external unfavorable conditions is known; by the ripening of the ten wholesome courses of action, the decline of ten external unfavorable conditions is known. There are ten benefits of making the <s>añjali</s> (reverential salutation) toward a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>caitya</s> (shrine); ten benefits of worshipping a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>caitya</s>; ten benefits of offering an umbrella; ten benefits of offering a bell; ten benefits of offering cloth; ten benefits of offering a seat; ten benefits of offering a vessel; ten benefits of offering food; ten benefits of offering a vehicle; ten benefits of offering shelter; ten benefits of offering drink; ten benefits of offering fruit; ten benefits of offering a garland; ten benefits of offering loose flowers; ten benefits of offering a lamp; ten benefits of offering fragrance —'

body.text: daśānuśaṃsāḥ pravrajyāyāḥ. daśānnśaṃsā araṇyavāse. dasānuśaṃsāḥ paiṇḍapātikatve. daśa vaiśāradyāni.
body.translated_text: ten benefits of going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>). Ten benefits of dwelling in the forest. Ten benefits of the practice of eating almsfood (<s>paiṇḍapātika</s>). Ten kinds of fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>).

body.text: uddeśaḥ karmavibhaṅgasya dharmaparyāyasya.
body.translated_text: Summary (<s>uddeśa</s>) of the <s>Karmavibhaṅga</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the classification of actions).

body.text: I. tatra katamat karma alpāyuḥsaṃvartanīyam? ucyate. prāṇātipātaḥ. prāṇātipātasya anumodanam. prāṇātipātasya varṇavāditā. amitramaraṇābhinandanam. amitramaraṇasya samādāpanam. amitramaraṇasya varṇavāditā. garbhaśātanam. garbhaśātanasya varṇavāditā. sthaṇḍilapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ yatra bahavaḥ prāṇino ghātyante mahiṣapaśuśūkarakukkuṭādayaḥ tasya yajñapravartakasya putrāḥ pautrāś cānye ca janāḥ phalārthino bhayabhītāś cānuvṛttiṃ kurvāṇāḥ sattvān nirghātayanti.
body.translated_text: I. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> that leads to short life? It is said: taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>); approving of the taking of life; praising the taking of life; rejoicing at the death of an enemy; inciting the death of an enemy; praising the death of an enemy; causing abortion (<s>garbhaśātana</s>); praising the causing of abortion; establishing a slaughter-ground (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) where many living beings are killed—buffaloes, cattle, pigs, chickens, and the like—and the sons, grandsons, and other people of the one who instituted that sacrifice, seeking its fruits or driven by fear, continuing the practice, slaughter beings.

body.text: a) yathā kāśmīrāyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ bhikṣuḥ kilārhann anyatarasmin gṛhadvāre tiṣṭhati. tasya gṛhasya pārśvena rājapathas tena paśū ravamāṇo nīyate. sa bhikṣus taṃ dṛṣṭvā hāhā dhik kaṣṭam iti vadati. puruṣās taṃ pṛcchanti. ārya kim ayaṃ hādhikkaṣṭam iti śabdaḥ. sa āha. na vaktavyam etad aśrāddhānām. kāryārthaṃ tu bravīmi. ya eṣa paśū ravamāṇo nīyate. anena purā vaṇigīśvareṇa bhūtvā sthaṇḍilaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam. sāṃvatsarikaś ca paśuyajñaḥ pravartitaḥ. tatrānena bahavaḥ paśavo ghātitāḥ. maraṇakāle ca putrān āhūya prāha. putrāḥ. yady asti mayi sneho ya eṣa mayā sāṃvatsarikaḥ paśuyajñaḥ pravartitaḥ. eṣa mayi kālagate 'nupravartayitavya iti. putrais tathāstv iti pratiśrutam. sa kālagatas tena mohajena prāṇātipātena
body.translated_text: a) For example, in the great city of <s>Kāśmīra</s>, a certain monk who was an <s>Arhat</s> was standing at someone's house-door. Along the royal road beside that house, an animal was being led away bellowing. That monk, seeing it, exclaimed, "Alas! How terrible! How wretched!" People asked him, "Venerable one, what is this cry of 'How terrible! How wretched!'?" He said, "This should not be told to those without faith. But I shall tell it for a purpose. This animal that is being led away bellowing—formerly it was a great merchant lord who established a slaughter-ground and instituted an annual animal sacrifice. There he had many animals slaughtered. At the time of death, he summoned his sons and said, 'Sons, if you have any affection for me, this annual animal sacrifice that I have instituted—after I have passed away, you must continue it.' The sons promised, 'So be it.' He died, and because of the <s>karma</s> of killing born of delusion

body.text: samanvāgataḥ svagṛhe paśuḥ pratyājātaḥ. sa tatra jātau jātau ghātyate. adhunā ekaṣaṣṭitamaṃ vāraṃ nīyate. atha sa bhikṣus taṃ paśuṃ karuṇāyamāṇa āha. svayam eva te sthaṇḍilaṃ kṛtaṃ svayam eva yajñaḥ pravartitaḥ bahavaḥ paśavaś ca ghātitāḥ. kiṃ ravase. sarvam idaṃ nirarthakam.
body.translated_text: he was reborn as an animal in his own house. There, each time he is born, he is slaughtered. Now he is being led away for the sixty-first time." Then that monk, feeling compassion for the animal, said, "You yourself created the slaughter-ground, you yourself instituted the sacrifice, and many animals were slaughtered. Why do you cry out? All this is fruitless."

body.text: b) yathaivaṃvidhaṃ sthaṇḍilapratiṣṭhāpanam. tathā yuddhadarśanam. yatra bahavaḥ sattvā ghātyante hastyaśvamanuṣyādayaḥ. yuddhapratibaddhānāṃ ca śastrāṇām abhinandanam.
body.translated_text: b) Just as establishing such a slaughter-ground leads to short life, so too does watching battles where many beings are killed—elephants, horses, men, and the like—and rejoicing in the weapons employed in battle.

body.text: c) yathā coktaṃ bhagavatā vaiśālyāṃ kālikasūtre. prāṇātipāta ānanda sevito bahulīkṛto niraya saṃvartanīyo bhavati. tiryagyonisaṃvartanīyo 'pi bhavati. pretaviṣayasaṃvartanīyo 'pi bhavati. yasmād alpaprāṇātipātasya vipāko manuṣyabhūtasya sato alpāyuḥsaṃvartanīyo 'pi bhavati.
body.translated_text: c) As the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said in the <s>Kālika Sūtra</s> at <s>Vaiśālī</s>: "<s>Prāṇātipāta</s> (taking of life), <s>Ānanda</s>, when practiced and cultivated, leads to rebirth in hell (<s>niraya</s>); it also leads to rebirth in the animal realm; it also leads to rebirth in the realm of hungry ghosts (<s>pretaviṣaya</s>). The minimum result of taking life, when one is reborn as a human being, is that it leads to short life."

body.text: d) tathā daśādīnavā nandikasūtra uktāḥ prāṇātipātasya.
body.translated_text: d) Likewise, ten disadvantages of taking life have been stated in the <s>Nandika Sūtra</s>.

body.text: idaṃ karma alpāyuḥsaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to short life.

body.text: II. tatra katamat karma dīrghāyuḥsaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. prāṇātipātān nivṛttiḥ. prāṇātipātanivṛttau varṇavāditā. tatra samādāpanam. tadvarṇavāditā. vadhyaprāptānāṃ manuṣyapaśusūkarakukkuṭādīnāṃ parimocanam. bhītānāṃ sattvānām abhayapradānam
body.translated_text: II. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> that leads to long life? It is said: refraining from taking life; praising such restraint; encouraging others therein; praising such encouragement; freeing those who are about to be killed—humans, cattle, pigs, chickens, and the like; giving fearlessness (<s>abhayapradāna</s>) to beings who are frightened

body.text: anāthānāṃ sattvānāṃ madhye kāruṇyacittatā. glānānāṃ sattvānāṃ madhye maitracittatā. anyeṣāṃ ca bālavṛddhānām. teṣām eva bhojanapradānam. pratigrāhakeṣu ca maitracittatā. yat pūrvoktaṃ kuśalapakṣeṇa yuddhadarśanādi. tathā stūpacaityavihārāṇāṃ śīrṇānāṃ pratisaṃskaraṇam. ataevoktam.
body.translated_text: having a mind of compassion (<s>kāruṇyacitta</s>) toward helpless beings; having a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitracitta</s>) toward sick beings, and toward the elderly and the young; giving food to those very beings; having a mind of loving-kindness toward recipients of gifts. Also, what was mentioned earlier on the wholesome side regarding watching battles and the like. And also the repair of damaged <s>stūpas</s>, <s>caityas</s>, and <s>vihāras</s>. Therefore it is said:

body.text:
akālamṛtyur na bhavet tasya
yo bhagnaśīrṇaṃ pratisaṃskaroti.
body.translated_text:
"Untimely death shall not befall the one
who repairs what is broken and decayed."

body.text: a) tathā bakapratyekabrahmasūtraṃ varṇayanti sma. tena kila ṛṣibhūtena pañcābhijñena tṛṣṇārtasya sārthasya pathabhraṣṭasya upari ṛddhyā varṣaṃ pātitam. tadarthaṃ ca bhagavatā gāthā bhāṣitā.
body.translated_text: a) Thus they narrate the <s>Baka Pratyekabuddha Sūtra</s>. It is said that he, having become a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) with the five supernatural powers (<s>pañcābhijña</s>), caused rain to fall by his supernatural power upon a thirsty caravan that had lost its way. For that purpose, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke this verse:

body.text:
tat te purāṇaṃ vrataśīlavṛttaṃ
svapnād vibuddho 'ham iha smarāmi.
body.translated_text:
"That ancient conduct of vows and virtue of yours—
I remember it here, as if awakened from a dream."

body.text: tatra ca sārthe bodhisattvaḥ sārthavāho 'bhūt.
body.translated_text: In that caravan, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was the caravan leader.

body.text: ya eṇīkūlej anatāṃ gṛhītām.
body.translated_text: "He who, at the bank of the <s>Eṇī</s> river, seized the captive—"

body.text: eṇī nāma nadī yasyā anukūle rājā kaścid gṛhītaḥ pratyamitreṇa
body.translated_text: The <s>Eṇī</s> is a river. On its bank, a certain king had been captured by an enemy

body.text: himavantam anupraviśya sa nīyamāna eva vadhyaṃ prāptaḥ sabalavāhanaḥ. tena ṛṣibhūtena ṛddhyā vātavarṣaṃ muktam. sa copāyena pratyamitrajanakāyo vibhrāmitaḥ. sa rājā mokṣitaḥ.
body.translated_text: and was being led into the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas). While being taken, he, together with his army and vehicles, was about to be killed. That sage, by his supernatural power, unleashed a storm of wind and rain. By this stratagem, the enemy forces were thrown into confusion, and the king was freed.

body.text:
tat te dvitīyaṃ vrataśīlavṛttaṃ
svapnād vibuddho 'nusmarāmi.
body.translated_text:
"That was your second conduct of vows and virtue—
I remember it, as if awakened from a dream."

body.text: sa ca rājā bodhisattvo babhūva.
body.translated_text: And that king was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text:
gaṅgāsrotasi nāvā gṛhītā
nāgena ghoreṇa ṛddhikena.
body.translated_text:
"In the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, seized by a boat
by a terrible serpent (<s>nāga</s>) of great supernatural power—"

body.text: sa ca tadā ṛṣir gaṅgākūle maharddhikaḥ pañcābhijñaḥ pratiśarati. tena ca kāyaḥ krandamāno jīvitena nirāśas tato mokṣitaḥ.
body.translated_text: At that time, that sage of great supernatural power and five superknowledges was dwelling on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. A group of people, crying out and despairing of life, was freed by him from that serpent.

body.text:
tat te tṛtīyaṃ vrataśīlavṛttaṃ
svapnād vibuddho 'nusmarāmi.
body.translated_text:
"That was your third conduct of vows and virtue—
I remember it, as if awakened from a dream."

body.text: tasyāṃ ca nāvāyāṃ nausvāmī bodhisattvas tena kālenābhūt. evaṃ vidhaṃ te trividhaṃ karma kṛtam, tato 'tīva dīrghāyuḥ.
body.translated_text: In that boat, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was the ship-owner at that time. Thus three kinds of such <s>karma</s> were performed by you, and therefore you have exceedingly long life.

body.text: b) yathā kecid ācāryāḥ kathayanti. bhagavān āha. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo jambudvīpe sarvajanapadamārī vartate sma. athānyatareṇa sattvenānyalokadhātau sthitena ṛddhimataḥ sakāśāc chrutam. yathā jambudvīpe sarvamārī pātiteti. tena kṛtapuṇyena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam.
body.translated_text: b) As certain teachers relate: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said, "Formerly, monks, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, a plague was afflicting all the lands. Then a certain being dwelling in another world-system heard from one possessed of supernatural powers that a universal plague had fallen upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. That meritorious being made a vow

body.text: jambudvīpe upapadyāhaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ vyādhipraṇāśāya jāyeyeti. sa tatropapannaḥ. ye ca sattvās tṛṣitās teṣāṃ pānīyena vyādhiṃ nāśayati. ye ca bubhukṣitās teṣāṃ bhaktena vyādhiṃ nāśayati. evaṃ yena yasyārthas tenaiva tasya vyādhiṃ nāśayati. na nāma tasya kiṃcid apy anauṣadhaṃ. yad yad eva gṛhya prayacchati tat tad evauṣadham. tasya jambudvīpakair manuṣyaiḥ sarvauṣadhir ekanāma kṛtam. atha bhikṣavaḥ sarvauṣadhivaidyarājo bahūnāṃ sattvasahasrāṇāṃ jīvitāni dattvā kālagataḥ. kālāntareṇa mithilāyāṃ rājakule upapannaḥ. tato 'pi tena mahādevabhūtena aśītikṣatriyasahasrāṇi dharmadeśanayā pravrajitāni. jambudvīpe 'śītivarṣasahasrāṇi manuṣyāṇām āyur na parikṣīṇam. tataś cyutaḥ kālāntareṇa kuśīnagaryāṃ māndhātā saṃvṛttaḥ. bhūyaś ca saptasūryopadeśe
body.translated_text: 'May I be born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the destruction of all beings' diseases.' He was reborn there. Those beings who were thirsty—he cured their diseases with water. Those who were hungry—he cured their diseases with food. Thus, with whatever each one needed, he cured that one's disease. There was nothing that was not a medicine for him; whatever he took and administered became medicine. The people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> gave him the single name <s>Sarvauṣadhi</s> ('All-Medicine'). Then, monks, <s>Sarvauṣadhi</s> the physician-king, having given life to many thousands of beings, passed away. After some time, he was reborn in the royal family of <s>Mithilā</s>. From there too, as the great deity (<s>Mahādeva</s>), he led eighty thousand <s>Kṣatriyas</s> to go forth through the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the lifespan of human beings did not diminish for eighty thousand years. After departing from there, at a later time, in <s>Kuśīnagarī</s>, he became <s>Māndhātṛ</s>. And again, in the discourse on the Seven Suns

body.text: sunetro nāma mānavo vijñeyaḥ. ahaṃ sa bhikṣavas tena kālena sarvauṣadhivaidyarājo 'bhūt. tasya karmaṇo vipākena mahādevasyāyuḥpramāṇaṃ yojayitavyam. māndhātṛsunetrābhyām apy evāyuḥpramāṇaṃ yojayitavyam. idaṃ karma dīrghāyuḥsaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: the man named <s>Sunetra</s> should be understood to be the same. I, monks, was at that time <s>Sarvauṣadhi</s> the physician-king. Through the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, the lifespan of <s>Mahādeva</s> should be reckoned. The lifespan of <s>Māndhātṛ</s> and <s>Sunetra</s> too should be reckoned in the same way." This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to long life.

body.text: III. katamat karma bahvābādhāsaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. khaṭacapeṭapradānam. khaṭacapeṭapradānasyānumodanam. khaṭacapeṭapradānasya varṇavāditā. teṣāṃ pradānena tuṣṭiḥ. mātāpitroś cittaśarīre pīḍākaraṇaṃ tathānyeṣāṃ pravrajitānāṃ śīlavatāṃ cittasaṃkleśaḥ. amitravyādhinā tuṣṭiḥ. amitravyādhivyutthānenātuṣṭiḥ. vyādditānām abhaiṣajyapradānam. tathāparijīrṇabhojanam. idaṃ karma bahvābādhāsaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: III. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to many illnesses? It is said: giving blows with fists and slaps; approving of giving blows with fists and slaps; praising the giving of blows with fists and slaps; satisfaction with such blows; causing physical and mental suffering to one's mother and father; likewise, causing mental distress to other renunciants who are virtuous; satisfaction at an enemy's illness; dissatisfaction at an enemy's recovery from illness; not giving medicine to the sick; and also eating spoiled food. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to many illnesses.

body.text: IV. katamat karma alpābādhāsaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. khaṭacapeṭapradānān nivṛttiḥ. tatra samādāpanam. tadvarṇavāditā. tadabhyanumodanam. glānānāṃ mātāpitṝṇām upasthānakaraṇam. tad apy anyeṣāṃ gṛhasthapravrajitānām. amitravyādhinānāttamanaskatā. tasya vyutthānena cāttamanaskatā. bhaiṣajyapradānam. parijīrṇabhojanaṃ ca. idaṃ karma alpābādhāsaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: IV. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to few illnesses? It is said: refraining from giving blows with fists and slaps; encouraging others in such restraint; praising such restraint; rejoicing in such restraint; attending upon one's sick mother and father; and likewise upon other householders and renunciants; being displeased at an enemy's illness; being pleased at his recovery; giving medicine; and eating wholesome food. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to few illnesses.

body.text: V. katamat karma durvarṇasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. krodhaḥ. upanāhaḥ mrakṣaḥ. pradāśaḥ. mātāpitror avarṇavāditā. anyeṣāṃ ca
body.translated_text: V. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to ugly appearance? It is said: anger; resentment; hypocrisy; malice; speaking ill of one's mother and father; and of others

body.text: gṛhasthapravrajitānāṃ bālavṛddhānām. stūpāṅgaṇacaityagṛhavihārāṇāṃ ca bhūmer aviśodhanam. stūpānāṃ pratimāṇāṃ ca dīpavyucchedaḥ. durvarṇānāṃ sattvānām avahasanam. tathā caukṣasamudācāratā. idaṃ karma durvarṇasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: of householders and renunciants, of the young and the old. Not cleaning the ground of <s>stūpa</s> courtyards, <s>caitya</s> shrines, and <s>vihāras</s> (monasteries). Extinguishing the lamps at <s>stūpas</s> and images. Mocking beings of ugly appearance. And likewise, impure conduct. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to being of ugly appearance.

body.text: VI. katamat karma prāsādikasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. akrodhaḥ. anupanāhaḥ. amrakṣaḥ. vastrapradānam. stūpacaityagṛheṣu ca sudhādānam. suvarṇapātra dānam. gandhalepapradānam. alaṃkārapradānam. mātāpitror varṇavāditā. āryāṇāṃ śīlavatāṃ varṇavāditā stūpāṅgaṇavihārāṇāṃ saṃmārjanam. satataṃ gṛhasaṃmārjanam. virūpāṇāṃ sattvānām anavahasanaṃ tathānyeṣāṃ bālavṛddhānām. tathā caukṣasamudācāratā.
body.translated_text: VI. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to being of pleasing appearance? It is said: absence of anger, absence of resentment, absence of irritability. The giving of garments. Plastering <s>stūpa</s> and <s>caitya</s> shrines with lime. Giving golden vessels. Giving fragrances and ointments. Giving ornaments. Speaking well of the complexion of one's mother and father. Speaking well of the complexion of the noble and virtuous ones. Sweeping the courtyards of <s>stūpas</s> and <s>vihāras</s>. Constantly sweeping one's house.

body.text: a) yathā āryasundaranandena kila krakucchande samyaksaṃbuddhe bhikṣusaṃghe jentākasnānaṃ kṛtam. tāṃś ca dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ prasāditam. bhūyaś ca suvarṇena haritālena pratyekabuddhastūpe lepo dattaḥ. idam api dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ prasāditam. abhirūpatāyāṃ ca pariṇāmitam. bhūyaś ca stūpe kriyamāṇe prathamaṃ chattraṃ kāritam. yathā paścimabhave sa eva vyākaroti.
body.translated_text: a) As, for example, the noble <s>Sundarananda</s> — during the time of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Krakucchanda</s>, he provided a steam bath (<s>jentāka</s>) for the community of <s>bhikṣus</s>. Seeing them, his mind was filled with faith. Furthermore, he applied a coating of golden orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) to a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> <s>stūpa</s>. Seeing this too, his mind was filled with faith. He dedicated the merit toward having a beautiful appearance. Furthermore, when the <s>stūpa</s> was being constructed, he first offered an umbrella.

body.text:
jentākasya ca snānena haritālasya lepanena ca
ekacchattrapradānāc ca prāptā me suvarṇavarṇatā.
body.translated_text:
Through the bathing in the steam bath, through the coating of orpiment,
and through the offering of a single umbrella, I have attained a golden complexion.

body.text: tathaivāyaṃ śobhitavān. idaṃ karma prāsādikasaṃvartaniyam.
body.translated_text: Thus has he been made resplendent. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to being of pleasing appearance.

body.text: VII. katamat karma alpeśākhyasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. īrṣyā. mātsaryam. parasya lābhenātuṣṭiḥ. parasya varṇavāditāyā atuṣṭiḥ. mātāpitroḥ paribhavaḥ. āryāṇāṃ śīlavatāṃ paribhavaḥ. tathānyeṣāṃ vyādhitabālavṛddhānām. hīne dharmahīne 'kuśalamūle varṇavāditā. bodhicittotpādasya nivāraṇam. tadabhyanumodanam. idaṃ karma alpeśākhyasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: VII. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to having little influence? It is said: jealousy, miserliness, dissatisfaction with the gains of others, dissatisfaction with the praise spoken of others, disrespect toward one's mother and father, disrespect toward the noble and virtuous ones, and likewise toward others who are sick, young, or old. Speaking well of what is inferior, lacking in <s>Dharma</s>, and rooted in unwholesomeness. Obstructing the generation of the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). Approving of that [obstruction].

body.text: VIII. katamat karma maheśākhyasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. anīrṣyā. amātsaryam. paralābhena tuṣṭiḥ. parasya yaśovarṇaśabdaślokaśravaṇena tuṣṭiḥ. parasya varṇavāditāyā āttamanaskatā. bhagavataś caityastūpakārāpaṇam. hīne dharmahīne 'kuśalamūle nivāraṇam. maheśākhyakuśalamūle samādāpanam. bodhicittotpādanam. sarvamaheśākhyakuśalamūle bodhicittotpādanam.
body.translated_text: VIII. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to having great influence? It is said: absence of jealousy, absence of miserliness, satisfaction with the gains of others, satisfaction upon hearing the fame, praise, reputation, and glory of others, delight at the good words spoken of others. Commissioning the construction of the Blessed One's <s>caityas</s> and <s>stūpas</s>. Preventing what is inferior, lacking in <s>Dharma</s>, and rooted in unwholesomeness. Encouraging the wholesome root of great influence. Generating the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>).

body.text: a) yathoktaṃ bhagavatā vārāṇasyāṃ pūrvāparāntake sūtre
body.translated_text: a) As spoken by the Blessed One in the <s>Pūrvāparāntaka Sūtra</s> at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>:

body.text: 'jitasya bodhisattvasya samuttejanaṃ kṛtam. mahate khalu te 'jita autsukyāya cittaṃ damayati. yad idaṃ saṃghaparihāpaṇāya. vakṣyatehi.
body.translated_text: The encouragement of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ajita</s> was made: 'Great indeed, O <s>Ajita</s>, is the eagerness with which you discipline your mind. This is for the protection of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. For it shall be declared:

body.text:
maitreyas tuṣitasurālayādhivāsī
prāptavyā divi bhuvi ceha yena pūjā
sa śrīmān daśabalatām avāpya śīghraṃ
lokānāṃ bhavatu śaśīva nityapūjyaḥ.
body.translated_text:
<s>Maitreya</s>, dwelling in the celestial abode of the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods,
by whom worship is to be attained in heaven and on earth,
that glorious one, having quickly attained the power of the Ten-Powered One,
may he become ever-worshipful to the worlds, like the moon.

body.text: idaṃ karma maheśākhyasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to having great influence.

body.text: IX. katamat karma nīcakulasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. stabdhatā. abhimānitā ca. amātāpitṛjñatā. aśrāmaṇyatā. abrāhmaṇyatā. akulajyeṣṭhāpacāyitā. mātāpitror apratyupasthānam. āryāṇāṃ śīlavatām apratyupasthānam. anyeṣāṃ ca gurusthānīyānām ācāryopādhyāyānām apratyupasthānam. nīcakulānāṃ satvānāṃ paribhavaḥ. idaṃ karma nīcakulasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: IX. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to birth in a low family? It is said: arrogance, conceit, ingratitude toward mother and father, lacking the virtues of an ascetic (<s>śramaṇa</s>), lacking the virtues of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, not honoring the elders of the family, not attending upon one's mother and father, not attending upon the noble and virtuous ones, not attending upon others who hold the position of teacher — <s>ācāryas</s> and <s>upādhyāyas</s>. Scorning beings of low family.

body.text: X. katamat karma uccakulasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. astabdhatā. anabhimānitā. mātāpitṛjñatā. śrāmaṇyatā. brāhmaṇyatā. kulajyeṣṭhāpacāyitā. mātāpitroḥ pratyupasthānam. āryāṇāṃ śīlavatāṃ pratyupasthānam. anyeṣāṃ ca gurusthānīyānām ācāryopādhyāyānāṃ pratyupasthānam. nīcakulānāṃ satvānām aparibhavaḥ.
body.translated_text: X. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to birth in a high family? It is said: absence of arrogance, absence of conceit, gratitude toward mother and father, possessing the virtues of an ascetic, possessing the virtues of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, honoring the elders of the family, attending upon one's mother and father, attending upon the noble and virtuous ones, attending upon others who hold the position of teacher — <s>ācāryas</s> and <s>upādhyāyas</s>. Not scorning beings of low family.

body.text: a) yathā ca bhagavatā sūtra uktam. yato bhikṣavaḥ kuśalaśīlavanto brahmacārinaḥ kalyāṇadharmāṇaḥ pravrajitā upasaṃkramanti pañca tasmin kule 'nuśaṃsāḥ pratyanuśaṃsitavyāḥ. katame pañca. iha bhikṣavaḥ upasaṃkrānteṣu śīlavatsu cittāni prasādayanti svargasaṃvartanīyaṃ
body.translated_text: a) As the Blessed One said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when virtuous, celibate, righteous renunciants approach, five benefits are to be expected in that family. What five? Here, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when the virtuous ones approach, they generate faith in their minds — this leads to rebirth in heaven.'

body.text: tad bhikṣavaḥ kulaṃ tasmin samaye pratipadaṃ pratipannaṃ bhavati. punar aparaṃ bhikṣavaḥ upasaṃkrānteṣu śīlavatsu abhivādayanti pratyuttiṣṭhanti. uccakulasaṃvartanīyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ. tasmin samaye pratipadaṃ pratipannaṃ bhavati. evaṃ sarvasūtraṃ yojyam. idaṃ karma uccakulasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, that family at that time has entered upon the path. Furthermore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when the virtuous ones approach, they bow and rise to greet them. This, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, leads to birth in a high family. At that time the family has entered upon the path.' The entire <s>sūtra</s> should be applied thus. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to birth in a high family.

body.text: XI. katamat karma alpabhogasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. adattādānam. adattādānasamādāpanam. cauryavarṇavāditā. tadabhyanumodanam. mātāpitror vṛttyupacchedaḥ. tathānyeṣāṃ vyādhitabālavṛddhakṛpaṇānāṃ vṛttyupacchedaḥ. parasya lābhenātuṣṭiḥ. paralābhāntarāyakriyā durbhikṣābhinandanaṃ ca. idaṃ karma alpabhogasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XI. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to few possessions? It is said: taking what is not given, encouraging others to take what is not given, speaking well of theft, approving of that. Cutting off the livelihood of one's mother and father. Likewise cutting off the livelihood of others who are sick, young, old, or destitute. Dissatisfaction with the gains of others. Obstructing the gains of others. Rejoicing in famine. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to few possessions.

body.text: XII. tatra katamat karma mahābhogasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. adattādānān nivṛttiḥ pareṣāṃ cādattādānān nivāraṇam. pareṣām adattādānanivṛttānāṃ samanumodanam. mātāpitror vṛttipradānam. āryāṇāṃ ca śīlavatāṃ vṛttipradānam. tathānyeṣāṃ vyādhitabālavṛddhakṛpaṇānāṃ vṛttipradānam. paralābhena tuṣṭiḥ. parasyālābhenātuṣdḥ. paralābhasamanumodanam. subhikṣābhinandanam.
body.translated_text: XII. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to great possessions? It is said: refraining from taking what is not given, preventing others from taking what is not given, approving of others who refrain from taking what is not given, providing livelihood to one's mother and father, providing livelihood to the noble and virtuous, likewise providing livelihood to others who are sick, young, old, or destitute, satisfaction with the gains of others, not obstructing the gains of others.

body.text: a) tad eva sūtraṃ yojyam. punar aparaṃ bhikṣavaḥ upasaṃkrānteṣu śīlavatsu dānāni dadanti puṇyāni ca kurvanti. mahābhogasaṃvartanīyaṃ bhikṣavas tat kulaṃ tasmin samaye pratipadaṃ pratipannaṃ bhavati. idaṃ karma mahābhogasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: a) The same <s>sūtra</s> should be applied. 'Furthermore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when the virtuous ones approach, they give gifts and perform meritorious deeds. This, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, leads to great possessions. That family at that time has entered upon the path.' This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to great possessions.

body.text: XIII. tatra katamat karma duṣprajñasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. ihaikatyo na parān pṛcchati. paṇḍitān. śramaṇān. brāhmaṇān. ko dharmaḥ kiṃ dharmaṃ kurvataḥ śreyaskaram iti. api tu duṣprajñān sevati. paṇḍitān parivarjayati. asaddharmaṃ dīpayati. saddharmaṃ vigarhati. saddharmabhāṇakānāṃ vaiśāradyopacchedaṃ karoti. saddharmabhāṇakānām abhiniveśena na sādhukāraṃ dadāti. asaddharmabhāṇakānāṃ
body.translated_text: XIII. What is the <s>karma</s> that leads to poor wisdom? It is said: here someone does not question others — the learned, ascetics (<s>śramaṇas</s>), <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — [asking] 'What is <s>Dharma</s>? What should one do that leads to well-being?' Instead, one associates with the unwise, avoids the learned, illuminates the false <s>Dharma</s>, disparages the true <s>Dharma</s>, cuts off the eloquence of those who teach the true <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: sādhukāraṃ dadāti. mithyādṛṣṭiṃ varṇayati. samyagdṛṣṭiṃ vigarhati. tathā pustakalekhakavācakānāṃ vṛttyupacchedaṃ karoti.
body.translated_text: gives approval [to wrong teaching], praises wrong view, disparages right view. Likewise, one cuts off the livelihood of scribes, copyists, and reciters [of texts].

body.text: a) sūtre coktam. unmattakasaṃvartanīyam ... karoti. saṃmūḍhakaś ca kālaṃ karoti. duṣprajñaś ca bhavati. yathoktaṃ nandikasūtre. pañcatriṃśad ādīnavāḥ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthāne yojayitavyāḥ. buddhe cāgauravo bhavati. dharme saṃghe cāgauravo bhavati. ataḥ śākyasūtraṃ yojayitavyam. yadā ca bhagavān kapilavastum āgataḥ sa madyapānadoṣān na kadācid bhagavantam upasaṃkrāntaḥ. caturbhiḥ sthavirair bhagavatā preṣitair gatvā vinītaḥ kālagataś ca. śākyaḥ pṛcchati. bhagavan. tasya kā gatir iti. bhagavān āha. ime 'pi ca me śākya bhāṣitasyārtham ājānīyur iti sūtraṃ
body.translated_text: a) And it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: '[Intoxication] produces the <s>karma</s> leading to madness... and one dies in a state of confusion. And one becomes lacking in wisdom.' As stated in the <s>Nandika Sūtra</s>: 'Thirty-five disadvantages are to be connected with the state of heedlessness through liquor, spirits, and intoxicants. One becomes disrespectful toward the <s>Buddha</s>, disrespectful toward the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s>.' From this the <s>Śākya Sūtra</s> should be applied. And when the Blessed One

body.text: yojayitavyam. yathā cūḍā panthako nāma bhikṣus tasya rājagṛhe prativasato bhagavatā gāthoddiṣṭā. sā ca varṣātyayena na śakitā grahītum. bhikṣavo vismayaṃ prāptāḥ pṛcchanti. bhagavan kasyaiṣa karmaṇo vipākena duṣprajñaḥ. bhagavān āha. kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe parinirvṛte eṣa āraṇyako bhikṣus tripiṭakas tatkālam abhūt. bhikṣūṇāṃ ca buddhapūjām akurvatāṃ buddhavacanam antarhitam. te bhikṣavas tasya samīpaṃ gatāḥ asmākaṃ buddhavacanam antarhitam. asmākam apy upadeśaṃ kuruṣvety anena mātsaryadoṣāt teṣām upadeśo na kṛtaḥ. evaṃ tacchāsanam antarhitam. tasya karmaṇo vipākenaiṣa duṣprajñaḥ. idaṃ karma duṣprajñasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: should be applied. As for the <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Cūḍāpanthaka</s>, while he was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the Blessed One instructed him with a verse. But even after the rainy season, he was unable to retain it. The <s>bhikṣus</s>, filled with wonder, asked: 'Blessed One, as a result of what <s>karma</s> is he so lacking in wisdom?' The Blessed One said: 'At the time of the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, this one was a forest-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s> who knew the three baskets (<s>Tripiṭaka</s>),'

body.text: XIV. tatra katamat karma mahāprajñasaṃvartanīyam. ucyate.
body.translated_text: XIV. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward great wisdom? It is said:

body.text: ihaikatyaḥ paripṛcchaka jātīyo bhavati paṇḍitāñ chramaṇān brāhmaṇān sevate duṣprajñān parivarjayati. saddharmaṃ dīpayati. asaddharmaṃ vigarhati dharmabhāṇakānāṃ vaiśāradyaṃ varṇayati. sahitabhāṣiṇāṃ sādhukāraṃ dadāti. ahitabhāṣiṇaṃ pariharati. samyagdṛṣṭiṃ varṇayati. mithyādṛṣṭiṃ vigarhati. masīpustakalekhanīpradānāni dadāti. na ca madyaṃ pibati. yathoktaṃ ca nandikasūtre. pañcatriṃśad madyapānadoṣā akuśalapakṣeṇa yojayitavyāḥ. idaṃ karma mahāprajñasaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: Here a certain person is of an inquisitive nature; he attends upon wise <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and avoids the foolish. He illuminates the true <s>Dharma</s>; he censures the false dharma. He praises the confidence of <s>Dharma</s>-preachers. He gives applause to those who speak what is beneficial. He avoids those who speak what is harmful. He praises right view; he censures wrong view. He gives gifts of ink, books, and writing implements. And he does not drink intoxicants. As stated in the <s>Nandikasūtra</s>: the thirty-five faults of drinking intoxicants are to be connected with the unwholesome side. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward great wisdom.

body.text: XV. tatra katamat karma narakopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. tīvraṃ praduṣṭacittasya kāyavāṅmanoduścaritam. ucchedadṛṣṭiḥ. śāśvatadṛṣṭiḥ. nāstikadṛṣṭiḥ. akriyādṛṣṭiḥ. matsarivādaḥ. akṛtajñatā. ānantaryam. āryāṇāṃ śīlavatām abhūtābhyākhyānadānam. idaṃ karma narakopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XV. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the hells? It is said: the intense misconduct of body, speech, and mind of one with a corrupt mind; the view of annihilationism; the view of eternalism; the nihilistic view; the view of non-action; miserly speech; ingratitude; the heinous sins (<s>ānantarya</s>); giving false accusation against noble ones who are virtuous. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the hells.

body.text: XVI. tatra katamat karma tiryagyonyupapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. madhyamaṃ kāyavāṅmanoduścaritaṃ vicitraṃ rāgasamutthitaṃ karma vicitraṃ dveṣasamutthitaṃ karma vicitraṃ mohasamutthitaṃ karma. mātāpitroḥ pravrajitānāṃ cākalpikapradānam. tiryagyonigatānāṃ satvānām avahasanam. tathā praṇidhānakarma yathā govratikakukkuravratikaprabhṛtīnāṃ praṇidhānam atropapadyeyam iti.
body.translated_text: XVI. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the animal realm? It is said: moderate misconduct of body, speech, and mind; various <s>karma</s> arising from desire; various <s>karma</s> arising from hatred; various <s>karma</s> arising from delusion; giving improper gifts to parents and renunciants; mocking beings born in the animal realm; and likewise vow-<s>karma</s> such as the vow of those who practice the ox-vow or the dog-vow and the like, with the aspiration 'May I be reborn there.'

body.text: a) yathā ca bodhisatvasya siṃha jātake 'vadānaṃ vaktavyam. yathā ca varṣākārasya brāhmaṇasya markaṭopapattiḥ. tadyathā
body.translated_text: a) As the story is to be told of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the lion <s>Jātaka</s>. And as was the rebirth of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Varṣākāra</s> as a monkey. As follows:

body.text: varṣākāreṇa brāhmaṇena sthaviramahākāśyapo bhikṣū rājagṛhasyoparimeṇa gṛdhrakūṭāt parvatād ṛṣigiripārśvaṃ vihāyasā gacchan dṛṣṭaḥ. tena praduṣṭacittena devadattājātaśatrusaṃsargād vāgduścaritaṃ kṛtam. eṣa śramaṇo vihāyasā gacchan parvatāt parvataṃ gacchati. tadyathā markaṭo vṛkṣād vṛkṣam eva. bhagavataḥ kathitam. varṣākāreṇa brāhmaṇena krodhajātena vāgduścaritaṃ kṛtam. tasya ko vipākaḥ. bhagavān āha. asya vāgduścaritasya vipākato varṣākāro brāhmaṇaḥ pañca janmāntaraśatāni markaṭo bhaviṣyatīti. tatas tena varṣākāreṇa śrutaṃ bhagavatā nirdiṣṭatvaṃ kila pañca janmāntaraśatāni markaṭo bhaviṣyatīti. sa saṃvignacittaṃ prasāditavān. tena bhagavān parinirvāṇakāle pṛṣṭaḥ. tasya karmaṇaḥ kadā parikṣaya iti. bhagavān āha. tāny eva pañca janmāntaraśatāni kiṃ tu rājagṛhe utpatsyase yathā jambvā jambudvīpe jāyate. yatroṣṭrikāmātrāṇi phalāni. yathā kṣaudramadhv aneḍakam evamāsvādāni.
body.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Varṣākāra</s> saw the Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, a monk, going through the sky from <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain above <s>Rājagṛha</s> to the slope of <s>Ṛṣigiri</s>. With a corrupt mind, due to his association with <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, he committed verbal misconduct: 'This ascetic goes through the sky, going from mountain to mountain — just like a monkey from tree to tree.' The Blessed One was asked: 'The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Varṣākāra</s>, having become angry, committed verbal misconduct. What is the ripening of that?' The Blessed One said: 'As a result of this verbal misconduct, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Varṣākāra</s> will become a monkey for five hundred lifetimes.'

body.text: tatropapattir bhaviṣyati. tato vyutthitasya te sugatir bhaviṣyati. yathā cittapradūṣaṇena siṃheṣūpapannaḥ. tadarthaṃ ca bhagavatā gāthā bhāṣitā.
body.translated_text: He will be reborn there. After rising from that state, he will have a good destiny. Just as through the corruption of mind he was reborn among lions. And for that purpose the Blessed One spoke this verse:

body.text:
dīrghā jāgarato rātrir dīrghaṃ śrāntasya yojanam
dīrgho bālasya saṃsāraḥ saddharmam avijānataḥ.
body.translated_text:
'Long is the night for one who is awake; long is a <s>yojana</s> for one who is weary;
long is <s>saṃsāra</s> for the foolish who do not know the true <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: idaṃ karma tiryagyonyupapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the animal realm.

body.text: XVII. tatra katamat karma yamalokopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. kruddhasya pratihatacittasya kāyavāṅmanoduścaritam. lobho viṣamalobho mithyājīvo jighāṃsitapipāsitasya kruddhasya kālakriyā. vastuṣv abhiṣaktacittasya kālakriyā.
body.translated_text: XVII. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the realm of <s>Yama</s> (the hungry ghosts)? It is said: the misconduct of body, speech, and mind of one who is angry and whose mind is obstructed; greed, excessive greed, wrong livelihood; dying while angry, hungry, and thirsty; dying with a mind attached to possessions.

body.text: a) yathā coktaṃ bhagavatā śatavarge āgame karmavibhaṅgasūtre.
body.translated_text: a) As the Blessed One said in the <s>Śatavarga Āgama</s>, in the <s>Karmavibhaṅgasūtra</s>:

body.text: tasya khalu punar ānanda pudgalasyānyajātikṛtaṃ vā karma pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati. maraṇakāle vā mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. idaṃ karma yamalokopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: For that person, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>karma</s> done in another life is present, or at the time of death there is wrong view. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the realm of <s>Yama</s>.

body.text: XVIII. tatra katamat karmāsuralokopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. sarvamṛdukāyavāṅmanoduścaritam. mānaḥ. abhimānaḥ adhimānaḥ. asmimānaḥ. mithyāmānaḥ. sukṛta kuśalāmūlam asuralokopapattipariṇāmitam. sarvotkṛṣṭarāgasamutthitaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ prajñāmukhena. idaṃ karmāsuralokopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XVIII. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the realm of <s>Asuras</s>? It is said: all mild misconduct of body, speech, and mind; pride (<s>māna</s>); conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>); excessive conceit (<s>adhimāna</s>); the conceit of 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>); false conceit (<s>mithyāmāna</s>); meritorious roots of well-done wholesome deeds dedicated toward rebirth in the <s>Asura</s> realm; all supreme immorality arising from desire, through the gateway of wisdom. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the realm of <s>Asuras</s>.

body.text: XIX. tatra katamat karma manuṣyalokopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. subhāvitā mandabhāvitāś ca daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ. katame daśa. trividhaṃ kāyakarma. caturvidhaṃ vākkarma. trividhaṃ manaḥkarma. idaṃ karma manuṣyalokopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XIX. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the human world? It is said: the ten wholesome courses of action, well-cultivated and mildly cultivated. Which ten? Threefold bodily action; fourfold verbal action; threefold mental action. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth in the human world.

body.text: XX. tatra katamat karma kāmāvacaradevopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. susamāptā daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ. idaṃ karma kāmāvacaradevopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XX. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the desire realm? It is said: the ten wholesome courses of action, fully accomplished. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the desire realm.

body.text: XXI. tatra katamat karma rūpāvacaradevopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. susamāptāḥ susamāhitās tato viśiṣṭatarāḥ paripūrṇā daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ. idaṃ karma rūpāvacaradevopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XXI. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the form realm? It is said: the ten wholesome courses of action, fully accomplished, well-concentrated, and more excellent than that, and complete. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the form realm.

body.text: XXII. tatra katamat karmārūpyāvacaradevopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ. ākāśānantyāyatanam. vijñānānantyāyatanam. ākiṃcanyānantyāyatanam. naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam. etāḥ samāpattayo bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāś ca bhavanti. idaṃ karmārūpyāvacaradevopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XXII. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the formless realm? It is said: the four formless attainments — the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>); the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>); the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyānantyāyatana</s>); the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). These attainments are cultivated and practiced repeatedly. This is the <s>karma</s> tending toward rebirth among the gods of the formless realm.

body.text: XXIII. tatra katamat karma kṛtaṃ nopacitam. ucyate. yat kṛtvā karma āstīryati jihreti vigarhati vijugupsati deśayati ācaṣṭe vyaktīkaroti.
body.translated_text: XXIII. Now, what is <s>karma</s> that is done but not accumulated? It is said: that <s>karma</s> which, having been done, one spreads out, is ashamed of, censures, is disgusted by, confesses, declares, makes manifest,

body.text: āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadyate. na punaḥ karoti. idaṃ karma kṛtaṃ nopacitam.
body.translated_text: and undertakes restraint for the future, and does not do again. This is <s>karma</s> that is done but not accumulated.

body.text: XXIV. tatra katamat karmopacitaṃ na kṛtam. ucyate. yat karma kāyena paripūrayitavyam. tatra praduṣṭacitto vācaṃ bhāṣate evaṃ te kariṣyāmīti. idaṃ karmopacitaṃ na kṛtam.
body.translated_text: XXIV. Now, what is <s>karma</s> that is accumulated but not done? It is said: that <s>karma</s> which should be fulfilled by the body — there, with a corrupt mind, one speaks the words 'I shall do this to you.' This is <s>karma</s> that is accumulated but not done.

body.text: XXV. tatra katamat karma kṛtaṃ copacitaṃ ca. ucyate. yat karma sāṃcetanikam.
body.translated_text: XXV. Now, what is <s>karma</s> that is both done and accumulated? It is said: that <s>karma</s> which is intentional.

body.text: a) yathoktaṃ bhagavatā.
body.translated_text: a) As the Blessed One said:

body.text:
manaḥpūrvaṅgamā dharmā manaḥśreṣṭhā manojavāḥ
manasā cet praduṣṭena bhāṣate vā karoti vā
tatas taṃ duḥkham anveti cakraṃ vā vahataḥ padam
manaḥpūrvaṅgamā dharmā manaḥśreṣṭhā manojavāḥ
manasā cet prasannena bhāṣate vā karoti vā
tatas taṃ sukham anveti chāyā vā anuyāyinī.
idaṃ karma kṛtaṃ copacitaṃ ca.
body.translated_text: This is <s>karma</s> that is both done and accumulated.

body.text: XXVI. tatra katamat karma naiva kṛtaṃ naivopacitam. ucyate. yat karma sāṃcetanikaṃ svapnāntare kṛtaṃ kāritaṃ vā. idaṃ karma naiva kṛtaṃ naivopacitam.
body.translated_text: XXVI. Now, what is <s>karma</s> that is neither done nor accumulated? It is said: that <s>karma</s> which is intentional but done or caused to be done in a dream. This is <s>karma</s> that is neither done nor accumulated.

body.text: XXVII. tatra katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo narakeṣūpapannaḥ paripūrṇaṃ nairayikam āyuḥ kṣapayitvā cyavati. ucyate.
body.translated_text: XXVII. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the hells, having exhausted the full lifespan of a hell-being, passes away? It is said:

body.text: ihaikatyena narakīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitam. sa tat karma kṛtvā nāstīryati. na jihrīyati na vigarhati na jugupsati na deśayati nācaṣṭe na vyaktīkaroti nāyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadyate bhūyasyā mātrayā hṛṣyati. prītim utpādayati. yathā devadattakokālikādayaḥ. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo narakeṣūpapannaḥ paripūrṇanairayikam āyuḥ kṣapayitvā cyavati.
body.translated_text: Here a certain person has done and accumulated hellish <s>karma</s>. Having done that <s>karma</s>, he does not spread it out, is not ashamed, does not censure it, is not disgusted, does not confess, does not declare it, does not make it manifest, does not undertake restraint for the future, and moreover rejoices greatly and generates delight — as in the case of <s>Devadatta</s>, <s>Kokālika</s>, and others. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the hells, having exhausted the full lifespan of a hell-being, passes away.

body.text: XXVIII. tatra katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo narakeṣūpapanno 'rdhanairayikam āyuḥ kṣapayitvā cyavati. ucyate. ihaikatyena nārakīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitam. sa tat kṛtvā nāstīryati na jihrīyati na vigarhati na jugupsate na deśayati nācaṣṭe na vyaktīkaroti. nāyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadyate. api tu na bhūyasyā mātrayā hṛṣyati. na pritim utpādayati. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo narakeṣūpapanno 'rdhanairayikam āyuḥ kṣapayitvā cyavati.
body.translated_text: XXVIII. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the hells, having exhausted half the lifespan of a hell-being, passes away? It is said: here a certain person has done and accumulated hellish <s>karma</s>. Having done that, he does not spread it out, is not ashamed, does not censure it, is not disgusted, does not confess, does not declare it, does not make it manifest, does not undertake restraint for the future; however, he does not greatly rejoice, and does not generate delight. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the hells, having exhausted half the lifespan of a hell-being, passes away.

body.text: XXIX. tatra katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo narakeṣūpapannamātra eva cyavati. ucyate. ihaikatyena nārakīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitaṃ ca. sa tat kṛtvāstīryati. jihrīyati. vigarhati vijugupsati ācaṣṭe. deśayati. vyaktīkaroti. āyatyāṃ saṃvaram āpadyate. na punaḥ kurute. sa cen narakeṣūpapadyate upapannamātra eva cyavati.
body.translated_text: XXIX. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, having been reborn in the hells, departs from them immediately upon being born there? It is said: here someone has performed and accumulated <s>karma</s> leading to hell. Having done it, he is troubled, ashamed, disgusted, and remorseful. He confesses it, reveals it, and makes it known. He undertakes restraint for the future and does not do it again. If he is reborn in the hells, he departs immediately upon being born there.

body.text: a) yathā rājājātaśatruḥ. tena devadattasahāyenānantaryakarma kṛtam. pitṛvadhaḥ. saṃghabhedaḥ. dhanapālamokṣaṇam. śilāyantramokṣaṇaṃ devadattasyādeśena. tasmād avīcinarakagamanaṃ śrutvā tena saṃvignena bhagavati cittaṃ prasāditam. śrāmaṇyaphalasūtre 'tyayadeśanaṃ kṛtam. pratisaṃdadhāti kuśalamūlāni. tena maraṇakāle cittaṃ prasāditam. asthibhir api buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ
body.translated_text: a) For example, King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>. He, with <s>Devadatta</s> as his companion, committed the deeds of immediate retribution (<s>ānantaryakarma</s>): the murder of his father, the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the releasing of the elephant <s>Dhanapāla</s>, and the releasing of the stone-mechanism on <s>Devadatta</s>'s instruction. Having heard that he was destined for the <s>Avīci</s> hell, he was deeply shaken and placed his faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. In the <s>Śrāmaṇyaphala Sūtra</s>, he made a confession of his transgressions. He re-established his roots of merit. At the time of death, his mind was filled with faith. Even with his bones, he went for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>

body.text: śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi. sa upapannamātra eva cyavati. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo narakeṣūpapannamātra eva cyavati.
body.translated_text: 'I take refuge [in the Buddha].' He departed immediately upon being born there. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, having been reborn in the hells, departs immediately upon being born there.

body.text: XXX. tatra katamat karma niyatopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. yat kṛtvā kvacid upapattau pariṇāmayati amutropapadyeyam iti. sa tatropapadyate.
body.translated_text: XXX. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> that leads to determined rebirth (<s>niyatopapatti</s>)? It is said: that which, having been done, one directs toward a particular rebirth, thinking 'May I be reborn there.' And one is reborn there.

body.text: yathā bhagavato jātake śyāmākajātakaprabhṛtiṣu praṇidhānavaśād upapattir varṇyate. idaṃ karma niyatopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>Jātaka</s> tales, beginning with the <s>Śyāmāka Jātaka</s>, rebirth through the power of a vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) is described. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to determined rebirth.

body.text: XXXI. tatra katamat karmāniyatopapattisaṃvartanīyam. ucyate. yat kṛtvā na kvacid upapattau pariṇāmayati amutropapadyeyam iti. yathā satvāḥ karmavaśād upapadyante. idaṃ karmāniyatopapattisaṃvartanīyam.
body.translated_text: XXXI. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> that leads to undetermined rebirth (<s>aniyatopapatti</s>)? It is said: that which, having been done, one does not direct toward any particular rebirth, thinking 'May I be reborn there.' As beings are reborn through the force of <s>karma</s> alone. This is the <s>karma</s> that leads to undetermined rebirth.

body.text: XXXII. tatra katamat karma deśāntaravipākam ucyate. yat karma tasminn eva janmāntare vā deśāntaragatasya vipacyate śubham aśubhaṃ vā. tat karma deśāntaravipākam. yathā bhagavān kathayati. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo jambudvīpe manuṣyāṇam aparimāṇam āyur bhavati. yathā rājño māndhātuḥ. athānyatarasmin nagare maitrāyajño nāma
body.translated_text: XXXII. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> that ripens in another place (<s>deśāntaravipāka</s>)? It is said: that <s>karma</s> which ripens—whether wholesome or unwholesome—in a later birth or when one has gone to another place. That is <s>karma</s> ripening in another place. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> relates: "Formerly, monks, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the lifespan of human beings was immeasurable, as in the time of King <s>Māndhātṛ</s>. Then in a certain city, there was a son of a caravan leader named <s>Maitrāyajña</s>

body.text: sārthavāhaputro babhūva. sa pañcaśatasahāyaparivṛta udyānaṃ gataḥ. taiś ca sahāyair uktaḥ. asmin nagare baṇijas tava pitaraṃ pūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā mahāsamudram avatīrya suvarṇabhūmiprabhṛtīni deśāntarāṇi gatvā dvīpāntarāṇi ca paśyanti. dravyopārjanaṃ ca kurvanti. vayam api tvāṃ pūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā samudram avatīrya dravyopārjanaṃ kariṣyāmo dvīpāntarāṇi ca drakṣyāmaḥ. tatas tena evam iti pratiśrutam. sa rātrau gatvā mātaram āpṛcchati. amba suvarṇabhūmiṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ. tasya mātāha. aparimāṇaṃ putra dravyaṃ gṛhe tiṣṭhati. na gantavyam iti. sa mātur vacanena nivṛttaḥ. sa bhūya udyānaṃ gataḥ sahāyair uktaḥ. tam arthaṃ vijñāpayāmaḥ. tena tathāstv iti pratiśrutam. sa bhūyo mātaraṃ gatvāpṛcchati. bhūyaś ca mātrā pādapatanān nivartitaḥ. evaṃ tṛtīyam api. sa kālāntareṇa bhūya
body.translated_text: He, surrounded by five hundred companions, went to the park. Those companions said to him: 'In this city, the merchants, with your father at their head, have crossed the great ocean, gone to <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s> (the Golden Land) and other distant lands, and seen other islands. They acquire goods. We too, with you at our head, shall cross the ocean, acquire goods, and see other islands.' Then he agreed, saying 'So be it.' At night, he went and asked leave of his mother: 'Mother, we shall go to <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s>.' His mother said: 'Son, there is immeasurable wealth in the house. You should not go.' He was turned back by his mother's words. He again went to the park, and the companions spoke to him about the matter, and he agreed saying 'So be it.' He again went and asked leave of his mother. And again his mother, falling at his feet, turned him back. Thus a third time also. After some time, he again

body.translated_text: went to the park and the companions said: 'Because of your fault, we too do not go. Let us set out; on the thirteenth day we shall depart.' Without his mother's knowledge, he had much merchandise taken out. At the time of his departure, as he was setting out, his mother stood at the door, falling at his feet, saying 'Son, you must not go.' Angered, he placed his foot on his mother's head and crossed over, and went to the ocean shore. He said to his companions: 'For those who cross the ocean, neither life nor death is certain. Let us all take the eightfold <s>poṣadha</s> (observance).' They agreed, saying 'So be it,' and took the observance. They crossed the ocean. When they had reached the middle of the ocean, their ship was destroyed by adverse winds and the like, and by that all perished. But <s>Maitrāyajña</s>, grasping a copper vessel tied to the mast of the ship, reached the ocean shore. Wandering about, he saw a city with golden ramparts, endowed with gardens, endowed with forests, endowed with lotus ponds, perfumed with incense, strewn with scattered flowers, hung with garlands of silk banners. From there four <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) came forth. They took him and led him into the city. With them he sported for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, many hundreds of thousands of years. They said to him: 'Noble son, this region of the earth is wonderful for you. You must not go out without our knowledge. If you do go out, you must by no means go northward.' After some time, he departed from there. Continuing on, he saw another city with silver ramparts, endowed with gardens and forests, as before. From there eight <s>Apsaras</s> came forth. They too took him and led him in. With them he sported for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, many hundreds of thousands of years, as before. After some time, he departed from there also. Continuing to wander, he saw a city with lapis lazuli (<s>vaidūrya</s>) ramparts, endowed with gardens, endowed with forests, endowed with lotus ponds, perfumed with incense, strewn with scattered flowers, hung with garlands of silk banners. From there sixteen <s>Apsaras</s> came forth. With them too he sported for many years, as before. They said to him: 'Noble son, this region of the earth is wonderful for you. You must not go out from this dwelling. If you do go out, you must by no means go northward.' After some time, he departed from there. Continuing to wander
