From there <s>apsaras</s> came forth. By them he was led inside. In the same way, with them too he sported for many years, many hundreds of years, many hundreds of thousands of years. body.translated_text: Having reflected thus, having paid homage to his mother and father with his whole being, and having made prostrations and a vow: 'Wherever I may be reborn, may I serve my mother and father!' — and 'Whatever beings are reborn in the individual hells, for the benefit of all of them I remain here. And whatever beings in the world are bound or liberated, homage to them. May they protect me.' Having said this, that hell-being remained there at that time. And having made a vow again, he spoke once more:

body.translated_text: b) Just as in the <s>Śyāma Jātaka</s>, when <s>Śyāmakumāra</s> was struck by a poisoned arrow... by the blessing-words of <s>Śyāmakumāra</s>'s mother and father, the arrow came out, the poison was destroyed, and the dead one was revived — in the same way, there was well-being for him too. Just as in <s>Vajra-Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Dhanaṃjaya Sūtra</s>, the noble <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'That <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, whose mother and father were equally honored and properly worshipped, they care for him with a virtuous mind.'

body.text: adhosī vatana putro dhārmikeṇa karmaguṇena na ca kiṃcit pāpaṃ karma karoti. sarvaṃ sūtraṃ yojyam. yathā ca śivālakasūtre bhagavatoktam. tam evaṃ gṛhapatiputra mātāpitarau pañcasu sthāneṣu pratyupasthitau pañcasu sthāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayataḥ. tasya punar gṛhapatiputra mātāpitṛbhyām anukampitasya puruṣapudgalasya vṛddhir evaṃ pratyāśaṃsitavyā.
body.translated_text: The son of righteous <s>karma</s> and virtuous qualities does not commit any evil <s>karma</s>. The entire <s>sūtra</s> should be applied. And as the Blessed One said in the <s>Śivālaka Sūtra</s>: 'In this way, O householder's son, the mother and father who have attended to one in five respects are established in five respects. For that householder's son who is cared for by his mother and father, only growth is to be expected for that person.'

body.text: c) sa tatra prītyāhāraḥ sthitvā paripūrṇeṣu ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasreṣu kālagataḥ.
body.translated_text: c) He, subsisting on the nourishment of joy there, having remained for the full sixty thousand years, passed away.

body.text: d) yathā rājājātaśatrur aparipūrṇa eva nairayikāyuḥpramāṇe cyutaḥ. abandhyatvāt karmaṇāṃ kadācid atīva śirorujā bhavati.
body.translated_text: d) Just as King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> passed away before the full lifespan in hell was completed. Because <s>karma</s>s are never barren, sometimes there arises exceedingly severe headache.

body.text: e) atra kṛtapraṇidhānasya maitrāyajñasya mātāpitṛśuśrūṣā vaktavyā. yathā śyāmajātake 'ndhau mātāpitarau hastibhūtena paripālitau. anyeṣu jātakaśateṣu ca.
body.translated_text: e) Here, regarding the one who made the vow of <s>Maitreya</s>-sacrifice, the service to mother and father should be described. Just as in the <s>Śyāma Jātaka</s>, blind mother and father were cared for by one who had become an elephant. And likewise in the other hundred <s>Jātaka</s>s.

body.text: f) atha bhagavān prāptakālaṃ bhikṣūn āmantrayate. syād evaṃ bhikṣavo yuṣmākam anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena maitrāyajño nāma sārthavāhaputro babhūveti. naivaṃ draṣṭavyam. ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena maitrāyajño nāma sārthavāhaputra āsīt. tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo mama vacanaṃ śraddadhānair buddhe sagauravair bhavitavyaṃ dharme saṃghe sagauravair bhavitavyam. mātāpitṛṣu ācāryopādhyāyeṣu sagauravair bhavitavyam. evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam. ya evaṃ deśāntaragataḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavati.
body.translated_text: f) Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> at the appropriate time: 'It may be, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, that you think someone else was the merchant's son named <s>Maitrāyajña</s> at that time and occasion. This should not be so regarded. I myself was at that time and occasion

body.text: yathā maitrāyajñena deśāntaragatena tasminn eva janmani pratyekasvargaṃ pratyekanarakaṃ cānubhūtam. ya evaṃ deśāntaragataḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavati. idaṃ karma deśāntaravipākam.
body.translated_text: Just as <s>Maitrāyajña</s>, having gone to another region, experienced in that very lifetime both a personal heaven and a personal hell. He who thus goes to another region and experiences happiness and suffering — this <s>karma</s> ripens in another region.

body.text: g) etad darśayati bhagavān. yathā mayi tathā mātāpitṛṣu. ācāryopādhyāyeṣu vacanakāriṇāṃ samo vipākaḥ iha loke paraloke ca. katham iha loke samaḥ karmavipāko bhavati. yathā śrāvastyāṃ daridrapuruṣo bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhuñjānaṃ dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ prasāditavān. tena mahāpuṇyasaṃbhāra upārjitaḥ rājyasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma kṛtam. tad eva ca mokṣabījam. tac ca jñātvā bhagavatā gāthā bhāṣitā.
body.translated_text: g) The Blessed One shows this: just as toward me, so toward one's mother and father, toward <s>ācāryas</s> and <s>upādhyāyas</s> (teachers) — the ripening of <s>karma</s> for those who follow their words is equal in this world and the next. How is the ripening of <s>karma</s> equal in this world? As, for example, there was a poor man in <s>Śrāvastī</s>,

body.text:
ye tatrābhyanumodante vaiyāvṛtyakarāś ca ye
anūnā dakṣiṇā teṣāṃ te 'pi puṇyasya bhāginaḥ.
etad eva gāthā samutthānam.
body.translated_text: This is the origin of the verse.

body.text:
manaḥpūrvaṅgamā dharmā manaḥśreṣṭhā manojavāḥ
manasā cet prasannena bhāṣate vākaroti vā
tatas taṃ sukham anveti chāyā vā anuyāyinī.
body.translated_text:
Mental states are preceded by mind, mind is their chief, they are mind-made.
If with a pure mind one speaks or acts,
then happiness follows one like a shadow that never departs.

body.text: tataś cyutaś ca deveṣūpapannaḥ. yathā ca tagaraśikhī nāma pratyekabuddhaḥ. durbhikṣe daridrapuruṣeṇa sūpaḥ pratipāditaḥ. sa ca tadahar eva tasmin nagare rājābhiṣiktaḥ. tataḥ kālāntareṇa pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ. ya eṣa sūtrantare paripaṭhitaḥ pratyekabuddhas
body.translated_text: Having passed away from there, he was reborn among the gods. And as for the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Tagaraśikhī</s> — during a famine, a poor man offered him a vegetable dish. On that very day, that man was consecrated as king in that city. Then, after some time, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>

body.text:
tagaraśikhī nāma. evaṃ tāvad bhagavati sāṃdṛṣṭikaś cittaprasādasya phalavipākaḥ.
h) kathaṃ mātāpitṛṣu. yathā maitrāyajñaḥ sārthavāhaputraḥ ācaturthaṃ pratinivṛtto mātur vacanena caturṣu mahānagareṣu pratyekasvargasukham anubhūtavān. tat tu tasya mokṣabījam. evaṃ mātāpitṛṣv api sāṃdṛṣṭikaḥ phalavipākaḥ.
body.translated_text:
named <s>Tagaraśikhī</s>. Thus indeed, regarding the Blessed One, the fruit and ripening of faith at first sight is visible in this very life.
h) How regarding mother and father? Just as the merchant's son <s>Maitrāyajña</s>, having returned for the fourth time at his mother's command, [visited] the four great cities.

body.text: i) kathaṃ bhagavati mātāpitṛṣu ca cittapradoṣeṇa narakagamanaṃ bhavati. ucyate. devadatto bhagavati cittaṃ pra ... to 'vīcau mahānarake patitaḥ. tathā sindhu viṣaye raurukaṃ nāma nagaram. tatra śikhaṇḍī rājaputraḥ pitaraṃ ghātayitvā narake patitaḥ. evaṃ bhagavati mātāpitṛṣu ca cittapradūṣaṇena narakagamanaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: i) How does one go to hell through malice toward the Blessed One and toward mother and father? It is said: <s>Devadatta</s> generated malice toward the Blessed One... and fell into the great <s>Avīci</s> hell. Likewise, in the <s>Sindhu</s> region there was a city called <s>Rauruka</s>. There, <s>Śikhaṇḍi</s>

body.text: j) tena kāraṇena kiṃ nāsti nānākaraṇam. ucyate. mahāntaṃ nānākaraṇam. bhagavān anekakalpaśatasahasropārjitakuśalamūlasaṃbhūtasaṃbhāraḥ anutpannasya mārgasyotpādayitā buddho bodhāya mārgaṃ deśayati. tasmin kṛtaḥ prasādo 'prameyaphalavipākaḥ ante ca nirvāṇam. mātāpitror mokṣamārgo 'viditaḥ. api ca na sarvaṃ mātāpitror vacanaṃ kāryam. santi kecin mithyādarśanopahatacittāḥ putrān bruvanti. ehi mām avasanaṃ naya. tava ca bhaviṣyati hitāya
body.translated_text: j) For that reason, is there no difference? It is said: the difference is great. The Blessed One, whose accumulations were produced by wholesome roots amassed over hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), is the discoverer of the unarisen path, the <s>Buddha</s> who teaches the path to awakening.

body.text: sukhāya mama ca. [prapāte māṃ pā]tayāgnau vā praveśayeti. tan naiva kartavyam. kiṃ kāraṇam. mātāpitarau ghātayitvāvaśyaṃ narakagamanam. ata eva bhagavatā pratiṣiddho na mātāpitṛghātakaḥ pravrājayitavyaḥ nāsti tasya pravrajyā nopasaṃpadā. nāsti phalaprāptiḥ. evaṃvidhaṃ varjayitvānyathā samasamā mātāpitara ācāryopādhyāyāḥ. kathaṃ ca samasamā. nanu bhagavatoktam. mātāpitroḥ putrasneho yāvad asthimajjām āśritya tiṣṭhaty ata eva mātāpitṛbhyām ananujñātasya nāsti pravrajyā. yathāryarāṣṭrapālaśoṇaprabhṛtayo bhagavatā mātāpitarāv ananujñāpya na pravrājitāḥ. adyāpi tān ananujñātān na pravrājayanti. yathā ca bhagavati pravrajite śuddhodanasya putraśokena cakṣuṣī antarhite. ucyate. mātāpitaraḥ pañca sthānāni pratyāśaṃsamānāḥ putram icchanti. śaṃvardhito no vṛddhībhūtān pālayiṣyati kāryaṃ ca kariṣyati dravyasvāmī ca bhaviṣyati. kālagatānāṃ ca pitṛpiṇḍaṃ dāsyati. kulavaṃśaś ca cirasthitiko bhaviṣyati. imāni pañca sthānāni pratyāśaṃsamānā mātāpitaraḥ putram icchanti. naivam ācāryopādhyāyāḥ. kevalam eva kāruṇyaṃ puraskṛtya katham asyā nādikālapravṛttasya saṃsāracakrasya paryantaṃ kuryād iti. yathā bhagavatā vinaya uktam. upādhyāyasya śiṣye putrasaṃjñā bhavati. śiṣyasyāpy upādhyāye pitṛsaṃjñā bhavati. evam anyonyaniśritāḥ sukhino bhaviṣyanti. evam ācāryopādhyāyāḥ samasamā mātāpitṛbhiḥ. yathā cakravartisūtra
body.translated_text: for my happiness. "Throw me from a precipice, or cast me into fire." That should never be done. Why? Because having killed one's mother or father, one inevitably goes to hell. Therefore the Blessed One prohibited this: one who has killed a parent should not be ordained.

body.text: uktaṃ bhagavatā. kasya karmaṇo vipākena rājā cakravartī hastiratnāny aśvaratnāni ca pratilabhate. dīrgharātraṃ rājā cakravartī mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vā svayaṃ vā skandhe vahati vā rathādibhir vāhayati vā. ācāryopādhyāyān svayaṃ vahati vāhayati vā. tasya karmaṇo vipākena rājā cakravartī hastyaśvaratnāni pratilabhate. anenāpi kāraṇena samasamā mātāpitara ācāryopādhyāyāś ca. api tv asty anyatra nānākaraṇam. gṛhasthānāṃ mātāpitṛ pravrajitāḥ pūjyāḥ. pravrajitānām ācāryopādhyāyā eva pūjanīyāḥ. yathā mahīśāsakā gotrāntarīyā vinaye 'rthotpattiṃ dhārayanti. yathāha bhagavān. na bhikṣavaḥ ācāryopādhyāyān anāpṛṣṭvā deśāntaraṃ gantavyam. kasmād. bhavati bhikṣavo jīvitāntarāyo bhavati brahmacaryāntarāyo bhavati pātracīvarāntarāyaḥ. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo maitrāyajño nāma sārthavāhaputra āsīd iti. etad evāvadānaṃ yathāvasthitaṃ vaktavyam. evam eva samasamā ācāryopādhyāyā mātāpitaraś ca. yathā coktaṃ bhagavatā. yo bhikṣavo mātāpitarau skandhena gṛhya jambudvīpaṃ paryaṭeta yogodvahanaṃ ca kuryāt caturṣu
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: by the ripening of what <s>karma</s> does a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) king obtain the jewel-elephant and jewel-horse? For a long time the <s>cakravartin</s> king carries his mother or father on his own shoulder, or conveys them by chariot and other vehicles.

body.text: dvīpeṣu hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ ca dadyāt. evam api mātāpitroḥ pratyupakāro na kṛto bhavati. yaś ca punar buddhe prasādayet. dharme. saṃghe. pañcasu śikṣāpadeṣu āryakānteṣu śīleṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet. evaṃ mātāpitṝṇāṃ putraiḥ pratyupakāraḥ kṛto bhavati. tac ca sarvam ācāryopādhyāyāḥ kurvanti. yathāha bhagavān dakṣiṇāvibhaṅgasūtre. yathānanda pudgalaḥ pudgalam āgamya buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati yathoktāni ca śikṣāpadāni vaktavyāni. tenānanda pudgalena tasya pudgalasya na śakyaṃ pratikartum. yad idam abhivādanapratyutthānamātreṇaivam api prativiśiṣṭatarā ācāryopādhyāyā mātāpitṛbhyām. yathā ca mahākātyāyanenāvantiprabhṛtayaḥ paścimajanapadā abhiprasāditāḥ. yathā cāryamadhyandinena kāśmīrāyāṃ pañca nāgaśatani vinīya deśo 'bhiprasāditaḥ
body.translated_text: were to give gold and silver in all the continents — even so, the debt to mother and father would not be repaid. But if one establishes them in faith toward the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, in the five training precepts, and in the virtuous conduct beloved of the Noble Ones — thus toward mother and father

body.text: anavataptasarasaś ca kuṅkumam ānīya kaśmīrāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam. tac cādyāpi lokopabhuktam. vihāraś ca kārito 'dyāpi ca tatraiva prativasanti. yathā āryagavāṃpatinā suvarṇabhūmyāṃ yojanaśataṃ janapado 'bhiprasāditaḥ. yathā ca pūrvavidehā āryapiṇḍolabhāradvājenābhiprasāditā vihārāś ca kāritā adyāpi tatraiva
body.translated_text: and having brought saffron from Lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, he established it in <s>Kaśmīra</s>. That is enjoyed by the people even to this day. And a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) was built, and even now they dwell there. Just as by the noble <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, a territory of a hundred <s>yojanas</s> was converted in <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s> (the Golden Land). And just as <s>Pūrvavideha</s> was converted by the noble <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s> and monasteries were built, and even now they dwell there

body.text: prativasanti. yathā cāryamahendreṇa siṃhaladvīpe vibhīṣaṇaprabhṛtayo rākṣasāḥ samaye sthāpitā deśaś cābhiprasāditaḥ. yathā cādhyardhaśatake sūtra āryapūrṇena śūrpārake nagare pañcopāsakaśatāni
body.translated_text: Just as by the noble <s>Mahendra</s>, in <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> (Sri Lanka), <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and other <s>rākṣasas</s> were established in the covenant and the land was converted. And just as, in the <s>Adhyardhaśataka Sūtra</s>, by the noble <s>Pūrṇa</s> in the city of <s>Śūrpāraka</s>, five hundred lay followers

body.text:
abhiprasāditāni. candanamālaś ca vihāraḥ kāritaḥ. yathā ca bhagavān pañcabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ sārdhaṃ vihāyasā tatra gato janakāyaś cābhiprasāditaḥ. api ca kim ekaikasya bhikṣor nāmagrahaṇena kṛtena yato bhagavān parinirva ... ntar yaḥ kaścid vinīto bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vopāsako vopāsikā vā sarve te bhikṣubhir eva vinītāḥ. yaś ca yenābhiprasāditaḥ sa tasyācāryopādhyāyāś ca eta .... ta bhagavān mātāpitaraḥ pañca sthānāni pratyanuśaṃsamānāḥ putram icchanti. ācāryopādhyāyās tu kāruṇyān nirvāṇaṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti. anenāpi kāraṇena mātāpitṛbhya ācāryopādhyāyāḥ prativiśiṣṭatarā
iti. ata evam āha bhagavān. mama bhikṣavo vacanaṃ śraddadhānair bhagavati paraḥ prasādaḥ kāryaḥ dharme saṃghe mātāpitṛṣv ācāryopādhyāyeṣu paraḥ prasādaḥ kāryaḥ. tad vo bhaviṣyati dīrgharātraṃ hitāya sukhāyeti. idaṃ karma deśāntaravipākam.
body.translated_text:
were converted. And the <s>Candanamāla</s> monastery was built. And just as the Blessed One went there through the sky with five hundred <s>bhikṣus</s> and the populace was converted. But what is the use of mentioning the name of each individual <s>bhikṣu</s>? Since after the Blessed One's <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, whoever has been disciplined — whether <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>upāsaka</s> or <s>upāsikā</s> — all of them were indeed disciplined by <s>bhikṣus</s>. And whoever was converted by whomever, that one is their <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) and <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor)... The Blessed One [said]: 'Parents desire a son expecting five benefits. But teachers and preceptors, out of compassion, teach the <s>Dharma</s> leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. For this reason too, teachers and preceptors are more distinguished than parents.'
Thus the Blessed One said: 'O my <s>bhikṣus</s>, those who have faith in my word should place the highest devotion in the Blessed One, in the <s>Dharma</s>, in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, in their parents, and in their teachers and preceptors. That will be for your benefit and happiness for a long time.' This is the <s>karma</s> that ripens in other lands.

body.text: XXXIII. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ sukhito bhūtvā paścād duḥkhito bhavati. ucyate. ihaikatyo dānaṃ yācitaḥ samānaḥ pūrvaṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratijānīte pramudito dadāti. dattvā ca khalu pratisārī bhavati. sa yadā manuṣyeṣūpapadyate. āḍhyeṣu mahādhaneṣu mahābhogeṣu kuleṣūpapadyate. paścāt tasya te bhogāḥ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti. sa paścād daridro bhavati. yathāryagopakaḥ. tena kila kakucchande samyaksaṃbuddhe bhikṣusaṃghasya godhenur dattā. sa paścāt parair garhito na sādhukṛteyaṃ datteti. tena cittaṃ pradūṣitam. sa yatra yatropapadyate tatra tatra mahādhano bhavati. paścāt tena cittapradoṣeṇa daridro bhavati. paścime bhave 'pi rājagṛhe nagare
body.translated_text: XXXIII. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it, having first been happy, afterward becomes unhappy? It is said: here a certain person, when asked for a gift, at first joyfully agrees and gives with delight. But having given, he becomes regretful. When he is reborn among humans, he is reborn in wealthy families of great riches and great enjoyments. Afterward, those enjoyments of his undergo exhaustion and depletion. He afterward becomes poor. As in the case of the noble <s>Gopaka</s>. He, it is said, in the time of the fully enlightened <s>Kakucchanda</s>, gave a milk-cow to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>. Afterward, blamed by others — 'This gift was not well done' — his mind became corrupted. Wherever he was reborn, there he became wealthy. Afterward, due to that corruption of mind, he became poor. In his final birth too, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>

body.text: 'nyatarasmin gṛhe pratyājātaḥ. tasya jāyamānasya mātā kālagatā. anena mātā māritā jāyamānena mūlanakṣatre jāto 'yaṃ mā nirmūlaṃ kulaṃ kariṣyaty amaṅgalo 'yam iti mātrā sārdhaṃ śmaśāne utsṛṣṭaḥ. tatrāpi ca mātur ekastanāt kṣīraṃ pragharati tenaiva puṇyānubhāvena. vivṛddhaś ca bhagavatāgatya pravrājitaḥ. etac ca sarvam anupūrveṇa bhagavatā bhikṣūṇāṃ kathitam. evam anena pūrvaṃ kṣīradhenuḥ prasādajātena dattā paścād vipratisārī saṃvṛttaḥ. tasyedaṃ karmaphahm. yas tv asau pūrvakaś cittaprasādas tad evāsya mokṣabījam. yathā ca campāyāṃ mahānagaryām īśvaro gṛhapatiputraḥ. tena bhṛtyānāṃ haste sarvaṃ dhanaṃ caturdiśaṃ bāṇijyāya preṣitam. tac ca sarvaṃ deśāntaragataṃ vinaṣṭam. sa ca parakarmakaraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ sukhito bhūtvā paścād duḥkhito bhavati.
body.translated_text: he was reborn in a certain house. As he was being born, his mother died. 'This one has killed his mother by being born; born under the root-constellation, he will uproot the family; he is inauspicious' — thus, together with his mother, he was abandoned in the cremation ground. Yet even there, milk flowed from one of his mother's breasts, by the power of his merit. Having grown up, he was ordained by the Blessed One who came to him. All this was told by the Blessed One to the <s>bhikṣus</s> in due order. 'Thus, this one formerly gave a milk-cow with a mind born of faith, but afterward became regretful. This is the fruit of that <s>karma</s>. But that earlier arising of faith in his mind — that itself is his seed of liberation.' And just as in the great city of <s>Campā</s>, there was a householder's son named <s>Īśvara</s>. He sent all his wealth in the hands of servants to the four directions for trade. But all of it, having gone to foreign lands, was lost. And he became a laborer for others. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it, having first been happy, afterward becomes unhappy.

body.text: XXXIV. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ duḥkhito bhūtvā paścāt sukhito bhavati. ucyate. ihaikatyo dānaṃ samādāya yācitaḥ samānaḥ pratijānīte. kṛcchreṇa dadāti. dattvā tu dānaṃ paścāt prītim utpādayati. sa yadā manuṣyeṣūtpadyate daridreṣu kuleṣūtpadyate. tasya paścāt te bhogā abhivṛddhiṃ gacchanti. atra cāniruddhasyāvadānaṃ vaktavyam. tena kila rājagṛhe
body.translated_text: XXXIV. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it, having first been unhappy, afterward becomes happy? It is said: here a certain person, having undertaken giving, when asked, agrees. He gives with difficulty. But having given the gift, he afterward generates joy. When he is reborn among humans, he is reborn in poor families. Afterward, those enjoyments of his increase. Here the <s>avadāna</s> (narrative) of <s>Aniruddha</s> should be told. He, it is said, in <s>Rājagṛha</s>

body.text: śyāmākataṇḍulabhaktam upariṣṭhasya pratyekabuddhasya piṇḍapāto dattaḥ. taddivasam eva rājñā tuṣṭenāṣṭau mahāgrāmā dattāḥ. tac ca paścimakaṃ dāridryam. yathā tasyaiva vyākaraṇaṃ pūrvāparāntake sūtre. yathā ca śrāvastyāṃ daridrapuruṣeṇa svajanaphalāni yācitvā kṣetraṃ nītāni karṣaṇārthe. tasya patnyā paragṛhe bhājanam ādhāya vrīhim ānīya bhaktaṃ siddham. atha bhagavatā śāriputramaudgalyāyanamahākāśyapasubhūtiprabhṛtayaḥ ete uktāḥ. amukasya gṛhapater gṛhe prathamaṃ bhaikṣyaṃ grahītavyam iti. te ca sarve yathānupūrvaṃ tatra gatāḥ. sarvaiś ca tasmād bhaikṣyaṃ labdham. atha paścād bhagavān api gataḥ. tayā striyā jātaprasādayā pariśiṣṭaṃ bhaktaṃ sarvaṃ bhagavato dattaṃ praṇidhānaṃ ca karoti. anena bhagavan kuśalamūlena mā me bhūyaḥ kadācid dāridryaṃ syād iti. tathāstv iti bhagavatā pratiśrutam. tadahar eva tasya mahānidhānaṃ prādurbhūtam. tac chrutvā rājāprasenajit tasmin gṛhe gataḥ. tenoktam. asmākaṃ pūrvarājabhis te dīnārāḥ sthāpitā iti. gṛhapatinā tasya tato gṛhyāñjalipūro dattaḥ. aṅgāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ. rājñā bhūyo gṛhapater dattāḥ. suvarṇaṃ saṃvṛttam. athā rājā prasenajid vismayajātaḥ. gatvā bhagavato nivedayati. bhagavān āha. puṇyanirjātā gṛhapater na grāhyā. sarvaṃ ca tadānupūrveṇa kathitam. evam eṣa yadā dātā bhavati duḥkhena yācitaḥ samānaḥ pratijānīte. duḥkhena
body.translated_text: gave a meal of millet rice as alms-food to a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Upariṣṭha</s>. On that very day, the pleased king gave him eight great villages. And that was his last poverty. As is his prophecy in the <s>Pūrvāparāntaka Sūtra</s>. And just as a poor man in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, having begged fruits from his own people, took them to his field for plowing. His wife, having placed a vessel in another's house, brought rice and prepared a meal. Then the Blessed One instructed <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, and the others: 'You should receive your first alms-food at the house of such-and-such a householder.' And all of them went there in due order. And from him all received alms-food. Then afterward the Blessed One also went. That woman, having generated faith, gave all the remaining food to the Blessed One and made a vow: 'By this root of merit, Blessed One, may I never again experience poverty!' 'So be it,' the Blessed One assented. On that very day, a great treasure appeared for him. Having heard this, King <s>Prasenajit</s> went to that house. He said: 'Those gold coins were deposited by our former kings.' But when the householder gave him a handful from that [treasure], it turned to charcoal. When the king gave [coins] back to the householder, they turned to gold. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s>, filled with wonder, went and reported to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'What is produced by the householder's merit cannot be taken.' And all of this was told in due order. Thus, when this one is a giver, being asked, he agrees with difficulty. With difficulty

body.text: dadāti dattvā ca cittaṃ prasādayati. tena hetunā pūrvaṃ daridro bhūtvā paścān mahādhano bhavati. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ duḥkhito bhūtvā paścāt sukhito bhavati.
body.translated_text: he gives, and having given, he generates faith in his mind. For that reason, having first been poor, he afterward becomes wealthy. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it, having first been unhappy, afterward becomes happy.

body.text: XXXV. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ ca paścāc ca sukhito bhavati. ucyate. ihaikatyo dānaṃ yācitaḥ sa prahṛṣṭaḥ pratijānīte prahṛṣṭo dadāti. dattvāpi ca prītimān bhavati. sa yadā manuṣyeṣūpapadyate. āḍhyeṣu kuleṣūpapadyate mahādhaneṣu mahābhogeṣu. atra bhadrike nagare miṇḍhakaprabhṛtīnāṃ caturṇāṃ dānapatīnāṃ vipāko vaktavyaḥ. taiḥ kila tagaraśikhī pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍapātena pratipādilaḥ. atra vinayāvadānaṃ vaktavyam. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ ca paścāc ca sukhito bhavati.
body.translated_text: XXXV. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it is happy both before and after? It is said: here a certain person, when asked for a gift, joyfully agrees, joyfully gives, and having given, remains pleased. When he is reborn among humans, he is reborn in wealthy families of great riches and great enjoyments. Here the ripening of the four donors beginning with <s>Miṇḍhaka</s> in the city of <s>Bhadrika</s> should be told. They, it is said, provided alms-food to the <s>Pratyekabuddha Tagaraśikhin</s>. Here the <s>Vinaya</s> narrative should be told. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it is happy both before and after.

body.text: XXXVI. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ pūrvaṃ ca paścāc ca duḥkhito bhavati. ucyate. ihaikatyaḥ kalyāṇamitra virahito bhavati. sa dānaṃ na dadāti. na ca tena kiṃcit pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavati. sa yadā manuṣyeṣūpapadyate daridreṣu kuleṣūpapadyate. alpānnapānabhojaneṣu. yathā śrāvastyāṃ daridradārakasyāvadānaṃ varṇayanti. śrāvastyāṃ kila bhagavān piṇḍapātaṃ paryaṭati. tadā ca śrāvastyām ikṣudvādaśī nāma bhavati. bhagavatā cekṣūṇi labdhāni. anyatarasmin gṛhadvāre daridradārakas tiṣṭhati. sa bhagavantam ikṣūṇi yācati. bhagavataikaṃ dattam. sa
body.translated_text: XXXVI. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person endowed with it is unhappy both before and after? It is said: here a certain person is devoid of spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). He does not give gifts. Nor has he done any evil <s>karma</s>. When he is reborn among humans, he is reborn in poor families with little food, drink, and sustenance. As they narrate the story of the poor boy in <s>Śrāvastī</s>: it is said that in <s>Śrāvastī</s> the Blessed One was going about for alms-food. At that time in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a festival called the 'Sugarcane Twelfth.' The Blessed One received sugarcane. A poor boy was standing at the door of a certain house. He begged the Blessed One for sugarcane. The Blessed One gave him one. He

body.text: bhūyo yācatiḥ bhagavān āha. vatsa. ucyatām. necchāmīti te bhūyo dāsyāmīti. sa prāha. mayā bhagavan na kadācin necchāmīty uktaṃ pūrvam. bhagavān āha. vatsa. ucyatāṃ necchāmi bhagavan sarvāṇi dāsyāmīti. tenekṣulobhān necchāmīty uktam. bhagavatā sarvāṇi dattāni. athāryānandaḥ pṛcchati. bhagavan kim idam. bhagavān āha. na kadācid eṣa ānanda rūparasagandhasparśādīnāṃ tṛptapūrvo 'bhavat necchāmīti vā na kadācid uktapūrvam. tad etasya vacanaṃ tasya necchāmīti hetubhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati. āha ca.
body.translated_text: He begged again. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said, 'Child, say it: "I do not want any more; I will give them to you."' He replied, 'But <s>Bhagavān</s>, I have never before said "I do not want."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said, 'Child, say: "I do not want, <s>Bhagavān</s>; I will give everything."' Out of craving for sugarcane, he said "I do not want." The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave everything. Then the noble <s>Ānanda</s> asked: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, what is this?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This one, <s>Ānanda</s>, has never before been satisfied with forms, tastes, smells, touches, and the like, nor has he ever before said "I do not want." That utterance of his, "I do not want," will become a cause for that.' And he spoke a verse:

body.text:
necchāmīty eṣa vyāhāro na kadācid udīritaḥ
kuto rūpāṇi śabdāś ca gandhāḥ sparśāś ca vai kutah.
ity evaṃ prārthayann eṣa nityaṃ bhramati bāliśaḥ
necchāmīti praharṣeṇa yaiṣā vāk samudīritā
hetur alpecchatā yaiṣā sa evāsya bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text:
The utterance 'I do not want' was never once spoken by him.
Whence forms? Whence sounds, smells, and touches?
Thus yearning, this fool forever wanders.
The words 'I do not want,' spoken with joy—
this seed of contentment with little shall become his cause.

body.text: idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pūrvaṃ ca paścāc ca duḥkhito bhavati.
body.translated_text: This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person is afflicted both before and after.

body.text: XXXVII. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgala āḍhyo bhavati matsarī. ucyate. ihaikatyenālpamātraṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavati śīlavati pātrabhūte na tu punas tyāgacittam abhyastaṃ bhavati. yadā manuṣyeṣūpapadyate. āḍhyeṣu kuleṣūpapadyate mahādhaneṣu mahābhogeṣu. tena dānaviśeṣeṇa yat tena punas tyāgacittam abhyastaṃ na bhavati sa tena karmaṇā matsarī bhavati. yathā śrāvastyāṃ
body.translated_text: XXXVII. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes wealthy but miserly? It is said: here someone has given a small amount of charity to the virtuous and worthy, but has not cultivated the mind of generosity (<s>tyāgacitta</s>). When he is reborn among humans, he is reborn in wealthy families of great riches and great enjoyments—by that particular act of giving. But because he has not cultivated the mind of generosity, by that <s>karma</s> he becomes miserly. As in <s>Śrāvastī</s>

body.text: hilliśālagṛhapater avadānam. sa kila pūrvajanmani matsarī bhavati. atha tasya gṛhadvāre tagaraśikhī nāma pratyekabuddha āgataḥ. tasya bhikṣā dattā. tena dṛṣṭvādīyamānā tena kṣavaṇaye na ca bhikṣā dattā. sa ca pravrājitaḥ paribhraṣṭaḥ. sa tena karmaṇā divyamānuṣyakāḥ saṃpattayo 'nubhūya śrāvastyām agrakulikaputraḥ pratyājāto matsarī kālagataḥ. tasya dravyaṃ rājñā prasenajitāputrakaṃ gṛhītvā śatavarge āgame prasenajitsaṃyukteṣu rājopakīrṇakaṃ nāma sūtram. prasenajid bhagavataḥ kathayati. iha bhagavann agrakulikaḥ kālagataḥ. tasya mayāputrakaṃ svāpateyaṃ gṛhītam. bhagavān āha. katīyaṃ mahārāja gṛhapater dravyaṃ gṛhītam. sa āha. śataṃ bhagavan śatasahasrāṇāṃ yad āhataṃ pariśiṣṭaṃ dravyam aparimitam anāhatam. bhagavān āha. idaṃ tasya mahārāja saptamam aputrakaṃ dravyagrahaṇam. yat tena tagaraśikhī nāma pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍapātena pratipāditaḥ. tad asya karma parikṣīṇam. anyac ca kuśalamūlaṃ na kṛtam. tenādya prathamāyāṃ rātryāṃ mahāraurave narake pacyate. tatra bhagavān gāthā bhāṣate.
body.translated_text: the story of the householder <s>Hilliśāla</s>. He was miserly in a former birth. Then a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Tagaraśikhī</s> came to his house-door. Alms were given to him. But upon seeing them being taken, he sneezed and did not give the alms. And he had gone forth but fell away from the monastic life. By that <s>karma</s>, having experienced divine and human enjoyments, he was reborn as the son of a chief family in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, was miserly, and died. His property, being without an heir, was taken by King <s>Prasenajit</s>. In the <s>Śatavarga Āgama</s>, among the <s>Prasenajit</s>-connected texts, there is a <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Rājopakīrṇaka</s>. <s>Prasenajit</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the chief householder has died. I have taken his property as it was without an heir.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'How much of the householder's property did you take, great king?' He said: 'A hundred hundred-thousands, <s>Bhagavān</s>—that is the collected property; the remaining uncollected property is immeasurable.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This, great king, is the seventh time his heirless property has been seized. Because he once supported the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Tagaraśikhī</s> with almsfood, that <s>karma</s> of his is now exhausted. And he created no other root of merit. Therefore, tonight, in the first watch, he is being roasted in the <s>Mahāraurava</s> hell.' There the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke a verse:

body.text:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ jātarūpaṃ gavāśvamaṇikuṇḍalam
dāsakarmakarā bhṛtyā ye cānye anujīvinaḥ
mriyamāṇasya nānveti nāpi ādāya gacchati.
yat tena kṛtaṃ bhavati kalyāṇam atha pāpakam
tad dhi tasya svakaṃ bhavati tac ca ādāya gacchati.
tasmāt kuruta puṇyānāṃ nicayaṃ sāmparāyikam
body.translated_text:
Wealth, grain, gold, cattle, horses, jewels, and earrings,
slaves, servants, dependents, and all other retainers—
none of this follows the dying one, nor does he take it with him.
Whatever he has done, whether good or evil—
that alone is his own, and that he takes with him.
Therefore, accumulate a store of merit for the hereafter,

body.text:
puṇyāni paraloke 'smin pratiṣṭhā prāṇināṃ smṛtā
gṛhe tiṣṭhati kāyo 'yaṃ śmaśāne priyabāndhavāḥ
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ caiva gacchantam anugacchati.
body.translated_text:
for merit is declared to be the foundation of living beings in the next world.
The body remains at home, loved ones at the cremation ground—
both good deeds and evil deeds follow the one who departs.

body.text: ayaṃ pudgala āḍhyo bhavati matsarī.
body.translated_text: Such is the person who is wealthy but miserly.

body.text: XXXVIII. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo daridro bhavati tyāgavān. ucyate. ihaikatyena pudgalena bahu dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavati. tiryaggateṣu manuṣyeṣu ca duḥśīleṣv abrahmacāriṣu. punaḥ punas tyāgacittam abhyastam. sa yadā manuṣyeṣūpapadyate daridro bhavati tyāgavān tena dānābhyāsena. yat tu tenāpātrabhūteṣu dānaṃ dattaṃ tena daridraḥ. yathā śrāvastyāṃ tatra vinaye tantravāyasya nidānaṃ varṇayanti. sa tyāgavān daridraś ca. punaḥ punas tyāgacittam abhyastam. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo daridro bhavati tyāgavān.
body.translated_text: XXXVIII. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes poor but generous? It is said: here a certain person has given much charity, but to those in the animal realm and to humans who are of poor conduct and not celibate. And he has repeatedly cultivated the mind of generosity. When he is reborn among humans, he becomes poor but generous—through the habitual cultivation of giving. But because he gave to the unworthy, he is poor. As in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s> narrates the story of the weaver. He was generous but poor. He had repeatedly cultivated the mind of generosity. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes poor but generous.

body.text: XXXIX. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgala āḍhyo bhavati tyāgavān. ucyate. ihaikatyena pudgalena bahu dānaṃ dattaṃ bhavati śīlavatsu pātrabhūteṣu. punaḥ punas tyāgacittam abhyastaṃ bhavati. sa tena karmaṇā yadā manuṣyeṣūpapadyate. āḍhyeṣu kuleṣūpapadyate mahādhaneṣu mahābhogeṣu. yat tu tena punaḥ punas tyāgacittam abhyastaṃ tena tyāgavān bhavati. yathānāthapiṇḍadena kila krakucchande samyaksaṃbuddhe jetavanaṃ niryātitam. vihāraś ca kāritaḥ. evaṃ kanakamunau samyaksaṃbuddhe kāśyape sarvārthasiddhe ca. bhūyaś ca maitreyasya suvarṇāstīrṇaṃ niryātayiṣyati. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgala āḍhyo bhavati tyāgavān.
body.translated_text: XXXIX. What is the <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes wealthy and generous? It is said: here a certain person has given much charity to the virtuous and worthy. And he has repeatedly cultivated the mind of generosity. By that <s>karma</s>, when he is reborn among humans, he is reborn in wealthy families of great riches and great enjoyments. And because he repeatedly cultivated the mind of generosity, he becomes generous. As, for example, <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>—during the time of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Krakucchanda</s>, he donated the <s>Jetavana</s> grove and had a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) constructed. Likewise during the time of <s>Kanakamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>. And again, he will donate a ground spread with gold for <s>Maitreya</s>. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person becomes wealthy and generous.

body.text: XL. katamasya pudgalasyāyuḥ kṣīṇaṃ na karma. ucyate. yaḥ pudgalo narakāc cyuto narakeṣūpapadyate. tiryagbhyaś cyutas
body.translated_text: XL. For which person is the lifespan exhausted but not the <s>karma</s>? It is said: a person who, having died in hell, is reborn in the hells; having died among animals

body.text: tiryakṣūpapadyate. yamalokāc cyuto yamaloke upapadyate. devebhyaś cyuto deveṣūpapadyate. yathā varṣākārasya brāhmaṇasya punaḥ punaḥ kālagatasya markaṭopapattiḥ. yathā kāśmīrāyāṃ pūrvoktasya gṛhapateḥ punaḥ punaḥ paśūpapattiḥ. yathā ca śrāvastyāṃ kaścid daridraḥ kuṭumbī kālagataḥ. tasya gṛhadvāre balīvardo vraṇībhūtena skandhena tiṣṭhati. sa gṛha āsaktacittaḥ kuṭumbī tasya balīvardasya skandhe kṛmiḥ pratyājātaḥ. upapannamātraś ca kākena bhakṣitaḥ. punas tatraiva kṛmiḥ pratyājātaḥ. sa evaṃ saptakṛtva ekadivasena kālagataḥ. upapannamātraś ca kākena bhakṣitaḥ. yathā cāryamahāmaudgalyāyano magadheṣu bhaikṣyaṃ paryaṭamāno 'nyatamagṛhadvāram anuprāptaḥ. tasmiṃś ca gṛhe gṛhapatiḥ patnīsahito matsyamāṃsaprakāreṇa bhojanaṃ bhuṅkte. putreṇa paryaṅkagatena kṛṣṇā cāsya kukkurī puraḥ sthitā. sa tasya matsyā sthīni kṣipati. atḥa sa gṛhapatir mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ dṛṣṭvāha. gamyatām ārya nāsti kāścid atra yo bhikṣāṃ dāsyati. sa khalu saṃprasthitaḥ. taśmiṃś ca gṛhadvāre deśāntarābhyāgatāḥ puruṣā vidvāṃsaḥ pūrvasthitāḥ te taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ prāptāḥ. aho āścaryam ayaṃ nāma ṛddhimatām agryaḥ yena nandopanandau nāgarājānau vinītau vaijayantaś ca prāsādo vāmapādāṅguṣṭhena kampitaḥ śakro vismāpitaḥ trisāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ nimeṣāntaracārī sa nāma bhikṣām adattvā visarjitaḥ. atha sthaviras teṣāṃ saṃvejanārtham āha. vatsa. naitad āścaryam. puruṣā ūcuḥ. atha kim anyad āścaryaṃ vismayakāraṇam. sa uvāca. ya eṣa gṛhapatir matsyamāṃsaprakārair bhojanaṃ
body.translated_text: is reborn among animals; having died in the world of <s>Yama</s>, is reborn in the world of <s>Yama</s>; having died among the gods, is reborn among the gods. As, for example, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Varṣākāra</s>, who after dying again and again was reborn as a monkey. As in <s>Kāśmīra</s>, the previously mentioned householder who was reborn again and again as a sacrificial animal. And as in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a certain poor householder died. At his house-door stood an ox with a wounded shoulder. That householder, his mind attached to the house, was reborn as a worm on the shoulder of that ox. As soon as he was born, he was eaten by a crow. Again he was reborn as a worm in the same place. Thus seven times in a single day he died and was immediately reborn and eaten by a crow. And as the noble <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, wandering for alms in <s>Magadha</s>, arrived at a certain house-door. In that house, the householder together with his wife was eating a meal prepared with fish and meat. His son was sitting on the couch, and his black dog was standing before him. He was throwing fish bones to her. Then that householder, seeing <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said: 'Go away, venerable one. There is no one here who will give alms.' As he was about to depart, at that house-door there stood travelers who had come from other lands, learned men. Seeing him, they were filled with amazement: 'How astonishing! This one who is foremost among those with supernatural powers, who subdued the <s>Nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, who shook the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace with his left big toe and astonished <s>Śakra</s>, who traverses the three-thousand-fold world-system in the blink of an eye—he has been sent away without receiving alms!' Then the Elder, in order to stir their sense of urgency, said: 'Children, that is not the astonishing thing.' The men said: 'Then what else is astonishing and a cause for wonder?' body.translated_text: This is the person whose lifespan is exhausted but not his <s>karma</s>.

body.text: XLI. katamasya pudgalasya karma kṣīṇaṃ nāyuḥ. ucyate. yaḥ pūrvaṃ sukhito bhūtvā paścād duḥkhito bhavati. pūrvaṃ yo duḥkhito bhūtvā paścāt sukhito bhavati. asya pudgalasya karma kṣīṇaṃ nāyuḥ.
body.translated_text: XLI. For which person is <s>karma</s> exhausted but not the lifespan? It is said: one who, having previously been happy, later becomes unhappy; or one who, having previously been unhappy, later becomes happy. For this person, <s>karma</s> is exhausted but not the lifespan.

body.text: XLII. katamasya pudgalasya karma kṣīṇam āyuś ca. ucyate. yaḥ pudgalo narakāc cyutas tiryakṣūpapadyate. tiryagbhyaś cyuto yamaloke upapadyate. yamalokāc cyuto manuṣyeṣūpapadyate. tataś cyuto deveṣūpapadyate. yathā śrāvastyāṃ vaṇikputra udyānaṃ gataḥ puṣpahetoḥ patnīvacanenāśokavṛkṣam ārūḍhaḥ. sā ca vṛkṣaśākhā viśīrṇā. sa pāṣāṇaśilāyāṃ patitaḥ kālagataḥ. tatra mahājanakāyo rudati. atha bhikṣavo divāvihāraṃ gatāḥ. taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃvignā bhagavato nivedayanti. bhagavann aho anityatā. atrodyāne gṛhapatiputro bālo 'bhuktabhogo 'śokavṛkṣāt patitaḥ kālagatah. tatra mahājanakāyaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ rauravasadṛśaś ca śabdaḥ śrūyate. bhagavān āha. eṣa eva bhikṣavaḥ gṛhapatiputraḥ pūrvaṃ mahāsamudre 'nyatarasmiṃ nāgakule upapannaḥ. sa tatra jātamātra eva strīsahitaḥ krīḍamāno garuḍenoddhṛtya bhakṣitaḥ. tatra nāgakanyā rudanti iha striyo rudanti. sa ca yasyāḥ striyā vacanenāśokavṛkṣam ārūḍhas tasyopary āghātaṃ kṛtavān. asyā doṣeṇāhaṃ vṛkṣam ārūḍhaḥ. kruddhaḥ kālagato narakeṣūpapannaḥ. asya pudgalasya karma kṣīṇam āyuś ca.
body.translated_text: XLII. For which person are both <s>karma</s> and lifespan exhausted? It is said: the person who, having fallen from hell, is reborn among animals; having fallen from the animal realm, is reborn in <s>Yama's</s> world; having fallen from <s>Yama's</s> world, is reborn among humans; having fallen from there, is reborn among the gods. As, for example, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a merchant's son went to a garden,

body.text: XLIII. katamasya pudgalasya puṇyāni ca kṣīṇāni āyuś ca.
body.translated_text: XLIII. For which person are both merits and lifespan exhausted?

body.translated_text: It is said: as in the case of the householder <s>Hilliśālī</s>. As the Blessed One said: 'Furthermore, O great king, for that householder, his wholesome <s>karma</s> has been exhausted and no other has been performed. Today, during the first watch of the night, he is being cooked in the <s>Raurava</s> hell.' As king <s>Prasenajit</s>, having fallen from his kingdom, arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. He

body.text: XLIIIbis. katamasya pudgalasya nāyuḥ kṣīṇaṃ [na] karma. api tu kleśāḥ kṣīṇāḥ. ucyate. śrotaāpannasya. sakṛdāgāminaḥ. anāgāminaḥ. pratyekabuddhasya. ayaṃ pudgalo yasya nāyuḥ kṣīṇaṃ [na] karma. api tu kleśāḥ kṣīṇāḥ.
body.translated_text: XLIIIbis. For which person is the lifespan not exhausted and <s>karma</s> [not exhausted], but the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are exhausted? It is said: for the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), and the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>. This is the person whose lifespan is not exhausted, whose <s>karma</s> [is not exhausted], but whose afflictions are exhausted.

body.text: XLIV. katamaḥ pudgalaḥ kāyena sukhī na cittena. ucyate. kṛtapuṇyaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ kāyena sukhī na cittena. yathā mahādhanabrāhmaṇagṛhapatayo rājā ca māndhātā. ayaṃ pudgalaḥ kāyena sukhī na cittena.
body.translated_text: XLIV. Which person is happy in body but not in mind? It is said: an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who has performed merit is happy in body but not in mind. Like the wealthy <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders and king <s>Māndhātṛ</s>. This person is happy in body but not in mind.

body.text: XLV. katamaḥ pudgalaś cittena sukhī na kāyena. ucyate. yathārhann apuṇyaḥ cittena sukhī na kāyena. yathārya śoṇottaras tena kila pūrvajanmani pratyekabuddhasya snāyato gomayapiṇḍakaḥ kapikacchumiśraḥ snānārthaṃ dattaḥ. tena karma vipākena kuṣṭhena śarīraṃ viśīryati. tathā hi gāthā bhāṣitā.
body.translated_text: XLV. Which person is happy in mind but not in body? It is said: an <s>arhat</s> without merit is happy in mind but not in body. Like the noble <s>Śoṇottara</s> — in a former birth he gave a ball of cow dung mixed with cowhage plant as a bathing agent to a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> who was bathing. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, his body was afflicted with leprosy.

body.text: XLVI. katamaḥ pudgalaḥ kāyena sukhī cittena ca. ucyate. arhan kṣīṇāsravaḥ kṛtapuṇyaḥ. yathā kaśmīrarājā dharmayaśaḥputro bakulaḥ. tathā hy asya siṃhanādaḥ. aśītir me āyuṣmanto varṣāṇi pravrajitasya na kadācid vyādhir bhūtapūrvaḥ. antataḥ śiro'rtimātram api. tena kila vārāṇasyāṃ gāndhikabaṇijā bhūtvā kakucchandaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saśrāvakasaṃgho glānabhaiṣajyenopanimantrito bhikṣuṇā cārhatā ekā harītakī gṛhītā. sa tasya karmaṇo vipākena nirābādhaḥ. ārogyaparamā lābhā uktā bhagavatā. yathā cāryāniruddhaḥ kathayati. tasya khalv āyuṣmantaḥ piṇḍapātasya vipākena saptakṛtvaḥ praṇīte trayastriṃśadevanikāye upapannaḥ saptakṛtvo manuṣyeṣu rājyaṃ kāritam. tasyaiva ca piṇḍapātasya
body.translated_text: XLVI. Which person is happy in both body and mind? It is said: an <s>arhat</s>, one whose outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) are exhausted and who has performed merit. Like <s>Bakula</s>, the son of <s>Dharmayaśas</s>, the king of <s>Kaśmīra</s>. For thus was his lion's roar: 'For eighty years, O venerable ones, since my ordination, not once has any illness occurred to me — not even so much as a headache.'

body.text: vipākenārhatvaphalalābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ lābhī. tathā hi tasya bhagavatā durbhikṣe pañca bhikṣuśatāni dattāni. tasya puṇyānubhāvena sarveṣāṃ divyam anantabhaktaṃ prādurbhavati. ayaṃ pudgalaḥ kāyena sukhī cittena ca.
body.translated_text: Through the ripening [of his merit], he obtained the fruit of <s>arhatship</s> and the requisites of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick. For the Blessed One gave him five hundred <s>bhikṣus</s> during a famine. Through the power of his merit, divine and limitless food appeared for all of them. This person is happy in both body and mind.

body.text: XLVII. katamaḥ pudgalo na kāyena sukhī na cittena ca. akṛtapuṇyāḥ pṛthagjanā utsannakulavaṃśā vastrānnapānavirahitāḥ paragṛheṣu hiṇḍanti. tathā vyādhibhiḥ kuṣṭhakṣayakāsajvarapāṇḍurogadadrupāmādibhiḥ parigatā hastapādavikalāś cakṣurvihīnāś ca. ayaṃ pudgalo na kāyena sukhī na cittena.
body.translated_text: XLVII. Which person is neither happy in body nor in mind? Ordinary persons without merit, whose family lineage has come to an end, destitute of clothing, food, and drink, wandering to the houses of others. Likewise those afflicted by diseases — leprosy, consumption, cough, fever, jaundice, skin eruptions, boils, and the like — with crippled hands and feet and deprived of sight. This person is neither happy in body nor in mind.

body.text: XLVIII. katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo 'pāyeṣūpapanno 'bhirūpo bhavati prāsādikaḥ snigdhakāyaḥ snigdhacchavir nayanābhirāmo darśanīyaḥ. ucyate. yaḥ pudgalo rāgasamutthitena dauḥśīlyena samanvāgataḥ apāyeṣūpapadyate. yathā mayūraśukasārikākāraṇḍavacakravākaprabhṛtayaḥ. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo 'pāyeṣūpapanno 'bhirūpo bhavati prāsādikaḥ snigdhakāyaḥ snigdhacchavir nayanābhirāmo darśanīyaḥ.
body.translated_text: XLVIII. What <s>karma</s> causes a person, though reborn in the lower realms of existence, to be handsome, of pleasing appearance, with a smooth body, a radiant complexion, delightful to the eyes, and beautiful to behold? It is said: a person endowed with misconduct arising from desire is reborn in the lower realms. Like peacocks, parrots, mynas, and

body.text: XLIX. tatra katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo 'pāyeṣūpapanno durvarṇo bhavati rūkṣakāyo ghoradarśanaḥ. ucyate. yaḥ pudgalo dveṣasamutthitena dauḥśīlyena samanvāgato 'pāyeṣūpapadyate. yathā siṃhavyāghrakākaśṛgālakṛṣṇasarpapretapiśācādayaḥ. idaṃ karma yena apāyeṣūpapanno durvarṇo bhavati rūkṣakāyo ghoradarśanaḥ.
body.translated_text: XLIX. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the lower realms, is ugly, with a rough body, terrible to behold? It is said: a person endowed with immorality arising from hatred is reborn in the lower realms — as in the case of lions, tigers, crows, jackals, black serpents, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating demons), and the like. This is the <s>karma</s> by which one reborn in the lower realms is ugly, with a rough body, terrible to behold.

body.text: L. tatra katamat karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo 'pāyeṣūpapanno durgandho bhavati jihmendriyo 'vyaktendriyaḥ. ucyate. yaḥ pudgalo mohasamutthitena dauḥśīlyena samanvāgataḥ apāyeṣūpapadyate.
body.translated_text: L. Now, what is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the lower realms, is foul-smelling, with crooked faculties and indistinct faculties? It is said: a person endowed with immorality arising from delusion is reborn in the lower realms —

body.text: yathā chuchundarīkṛmyajagarayūkāmakṣikādayo yathā śarīre viṃśatikṛmijātayaḥ. idaṃ karma yena samanvāgataḥ pudgalo 'pāyeṣūpapanno durgandho bhavati jihmendriyo 'vyaktendriyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — as in the case of musk-rats, worms, pythons, lice, flies, and the like, and the twenty types of worms in the body. This is the <s>karma</s> by which a person, reborn in the lower realms, is foul-smelling, with crooked faculties and indistinct faculties.

body.text: LI. daśākuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ. katame daśa. trividhaṃ kāyakarma. caturvidhaṃ vākkarma. trividhaṃ manaskarma. eṣāṃ daśānām akuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ vipākena daśānāṃ bāhyānāṃ bhāvānām abhivṛddhir bhavati.
body.translated_text: LI. The ten unwholesome courses of action (<s>akuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ</s>). Which ten? Threefold bodily action, fourfold verbal action, threefold mental action. By the ripening of these ten unwholesome courses of action, the increase of ten external unfavorable conditions occurs.

body.text: LII. prāṇātipātasyākuśalakarmapathasya vipākena pṛthivyā ojaś ca tejaś cāntardhīyate. tasyaiva ca karmaṇo vipākenālpāyur bhavati.
body.translated_text: LII. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), the vitality and energy of the earth disappear. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one becomes short-lived.

body.text: LIII. adattādānasyākuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena pṛthivyām aśaniśukaśalabhamūṣikakīṭaprabhṛtayaḥ sasyaghāsakā utpadyante. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākena bhogavyasanam adhigacchati.
body.translated_text: LIII. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of stealing (<s>adattādāna</s>), crop-destroyers such as lightning, parrots, locusts, mice, beetles, and the like arise on the earth. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one experiences loss of wealth.

body.text: LIV. kāmamithyācārasyākuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena pṛthivyāṃ tṛṇadarbhādīni durgandhīni prādurbhavanti. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākena saṃpannagṛhāvāsaṃ praviśanti. atrāvadānaṃ śvabhrapadasya susudhī dārikā kāsirājñaḥ patnī devāvataraṇe kālodayinaḥ pūrvajanmany avadānaṃ vaktavyam.
body.translated_text: LIV. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>), foul-smelling things such as coarse grasses and <s>darbha</s> grass appear on the earth. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, they enter well-established households. Here the stories of <s>Śvabhrapada</s>, the maiden <s>Susudhī</s> wife of King <s>Kāśi</s>, and the past-life story of <s>Kālodayin</s> at the <s>Devāvataraṇa</s> should be told.

body.text: LV. mṛṣāvādasyākuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena mukharogadantarogagalarogamukhadaurgandhyādīni
body.translated_text: LV. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), mouth diseases, tooth diseases, throat diseases, foul breath, and the like

body.text: prādurbhavanti. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākenābhūtākhyānaṃ pratilabhate.
body.translated_text: appear. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one receives false accusations.

body.text: LVI. piśunavacanasyākuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena pṛthivyāṃ śarkarakaṭhallyādīni duḥkhasaṃsparśādīni prādurbhavanti. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākena jātivyasanā mitravyasanā bhavanti bhedyaḥ parivāraś ca bhavati.
body.translated_text: LVI. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of slander (<s>piśunavacana</s>), gravel, thorns, and other things painful to touch appear on the earth. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one has family misfortunes and friend misfortunes, and one's retinue becomes divisible.

body.text: LVIl. paruṣavacaso 'kuśalakarmapathasya vipākena pāṃśurajodhūlivātavṛṣṭyādīni prādurbhavanti. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākenāmanojñaśabdaśravaṇadarśanāny anubhavanti.
body.translated_text: LVII. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of harsh speech (<s>paruṣavacas</s>), dust, dirt, wind-storms, and the like appear. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one experiences the hearing and seeing of unpleasant sounds and sights.

body.text: LVIII. saṃbhinnapralāpasyākuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena ... kandaraśvabhrādīni prādurbhavanti. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākenānādeyavacanā bhavanti.
body.translated_text: LVIII. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of frivolous talk (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>), ... gorges, ravines, and the like appear. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one's words carry no weight.

body.text: LIX. abhidhyāyā akuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena vrīhiyavagodhūmādīnāṃ sasyānāṃ tuṣapalālādīni prādurbhavanti. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākena paraprārthanīyabhogā bhavanti.
body.translated_text: LIX. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), husks, chaff, and the like of rice, barley, wheat, and other crops appear. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one's wealth becomes desired by others.

body.text: LX. vyāpādasyākuśalakarmapathasya vipākena prabhūte upte niṣphalaṃ sasyaṃ bhavati. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākena pratikūladarśano bhavati.
body.translated_text: LX. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), when much is sown, the crops become fruitless. By the ripening of that same <s>karma</s>, one becomes repulsive in appearance.

body.text: LXI. mithyādṛṣṭer akuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena tiktakaṭukabhāvāny
body.translated_text: LXI. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), bitter and pungent things —

body.text: api picumandakoṣātakīviṣatiktālābuprabhṛtīni phalāni prādurbhavanti. mithyādṛṣṭer akuśalasya karmapathasya vipākena nāstikyavādī bhavati. ucchedadṛṣṭiḥ lokāyatādiṣu ca śāstreṣu prasādo bhavati. yathā padāśvasya rājaputrasya yaḥ kumārakāśyapena śvetikāyāṃ vinīto lokāyatikaḥ. yathā yathā sattvā imān daśākuśalān karmapathān bhāvayanti tathaiṣāṃ daśānāṃ bāhyānāṃ bhāvānām atīva prādurbhāvo bhavati. anenaiva ca kāraṇena mahāsaṃvartakalpe bhaviṣyati samayo 'nāgate 'dhvani yat tilā bhaviṣyanti tilapiṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati tailaṃ na bhaviṣyati ikṣur bhaviṣyati ikṣuraso na bhaviṣyati guḍo na bhaviṣyati. na khaṇḍaṃ bhaviṣyati na śarkarā bhaviṣyanti. gāvo bhaviṣyanti kṣīraṃ bhaviṣyati dadhi bhaviṣyati navanītaṃ na bhaviṣyati na ghṛtaṃ na gḥrtamaṇḍo bhaviṣyati. evam anupūrveṇa sarveṇa sarve rasā antardhāsyanti.
body.translated_text: — such as <s>neem</s> (<s>picumanda</s>), <s>bitter gourd</s> (<s>koṣātakī</s>), <s>poisonous bitter gourd</s> (<s>viṣatiktālābu</s>), and the like fruits appear. By the ripening of the unwholesome course of action of wrong view, one becomes a nihilist, holds the annihilationist view, and has faith in <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialism) and other such treatises — as in the case of Prince <s>Padāśva</s>, who was the <s>Lokāyatika</s> converted by <s>Kumārakāśyapa</s> at <s>Śvetikā</s>. To the extent that beings cultivate these ten unwholesome courses of action, to that extent these ten external unfavorable conditions excessively manifest. And for this very reason, in the great dissolution (<s>mahāsaṃvarta</s>) era, there will come a time in the future when sesame will exist but sesame paste will exist and oil will not; sugarcane will exist but sugarcane juice will not, jaggery will not, sugar candy will not, crystal sugar will not; cows will exist, milk will exist, curd will exist, but butter will not, ghee will not, cream of ghee will not. Thus gradually all flavors will completely disappear.

body.text: [notes only]
body.translated_text: [editorial notes]

body.text: LXII. katame daśānuśaṃsā madhyadeśe caturmahācaityalumbinīmahābodhiprabhṛtiṣu tathāgatacaityāñjalikarmapraṇipāte. ucyate. madhyadeśe janma pratilabhate. udārāṇi ca vastrāṇi pratilabhate. udāraṃ kulaṃ pratilabhate. udāraṃ vayaḥ pratilabhate. udāraṃ svaraṃ pratilabhate. udārāṃ pratibhānatāṃ pratilabhate. udārāṃ śraddhāṃ pratilabhate. udāraṃ śīlaṃ pratilabhate. udāraṃ śrutaṃ pratilabhate. udāraṃ tyāgaṃ pratilabhate. udārāṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabhate. udārāṃ prajñāṃ pratilabhate. asyoddānam. deśavastrakularūpasvarapratibhānatāśraddhāśīlaśrutatyāgān smṛtimān bhavati prajñāvān tathāgatasya buddhaprasādaṃ kṛtvāñjaliṃ labhate dhīraḥ
body.translated_text: LXII. What are the ten benefits of making the <s>añjali</s> (reverential salutation) and prostration at the four great <s>caityas</s> (shrines) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the Middle Country — <s>Lumbinī</s>, <s>Mahābodhi</s>, and the others? It is said: one obtains birth in the Middle Country; one obtains excellent garments; one obtains an excellent family; one obtains excellent age; one obtains an excellent voice; one obtains excellent eloquence; one obtains excellent faith; one obtains excellent morality; one obtains excellent learning; one obtains excellent generosity; one obtains excellent mindfulness; one obtains excellent wisdom. The summary verse: 'The steadfast one, having made the <s>añjali</s> with faith toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, obtains country, garments, family, beauty, voice, eloquence, faith, morality, learning, and generosity; becomes mindful and wise,

body.text: saprajña udāram āśravakṣayam. uktaṃ ca sūtre. ye kecid ānanda caityacaryāṃ caramāṇāḥ prasannacittāḥ kālaṃ kariṣyanti. yathā bhallo nikṣiptaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhate evaṃ kāyasya bhedāt svargeṣūpapatsyanti.
body.translated_text: the wise one obtains the excellent destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements).' And it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, performing the <s>caitya</s>-practice with a clear mind, will die — just as an arrow released stands upon the earth — so at the breaking up of the body, they will be reborn in the heavens.'

body.text: LXIII. katame daśānuśaṃsās tathāgatacaityavandanāyām. ucyate. abhirūpo bhavati. susvaraḥ. ādeyavākyaḥ. pariṣadam upasaṃkrāntaḥ pariṣadam āvarjayati priyo bhavati devamanuṣyāṇām. maheśākhyo bhavati. maheśākhyaiḥ samāgamo sattvaiḥ bhavati. buddhair buddhaśrāvakaiś ca samāgamo bhavati. mahābhogo bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti. ime daśānuśāṃsās tathāgatacaityavandanāyāḥ.
body.translated_text: LXIII. What are the ten benefits of worshipping a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>caitya</s>? It is said: one becomes beautiful; one becomes sweet-voiced; one's words carry weight; when one approaches an assembly, one wins over the assembly; one becomes dear to gods and humans; one becomes of great influence; one meets with beings of great influence; one meets with <s>Buddhas</s> and disciples of <s>Buddhas</s>; one becomes of great wealth; one is reborn in the heavens; and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). These are the ten benefits of worshipping a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>caitya</s>.

body.text: LXIV. katame daśānuśaṃsāś chattrapradānasya. ucyate. chattrabhūto bhavati lokasya. anavatapto bhavati kāyena anavatapto bhavati cittena. ādhipatyasaṃvartanīyaṃ cānena karma kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitam. punaḥ punaś ca rājā bhavati cakravartī. maheśākhyo bhavati. maheśākhyaiḥ sattvaiḥ samāgamo bhavati buddhair buddhaśrāvakaiś ca samāgamo bhavati. mahābhogo bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXIV. What are the ten benefits of offering an umbrella (<s>chattra</s>)? It is said: one becomes a protector of the world, like an umbrella; one is not heated in body; one is not heated in mind; one has done and accumulated <s>karma</s> tending toward sovereignty; again and again one becomes a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king; one becomes of great influence; one meets with beings of great influence; one meets with <s>Buddhas</s> and disciples of <s>Buddhas</s>; one becomes of great wealth; one is reborn in the heavens; and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) atra gaṅgāsaṃtāre bhagavataḥ pratyekabuddhasya stūpe dattasya chattrasya vipāko varṇyate. yathā cāryasundaranando vyākaroti.
body.translated_text: a) Here the ripening of an umbrella offered at the <s>stūpa</s> of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> at the Ganges crossing is described. As the Noble <s>Sundarananda</s> declares:

body.text:
jentākasya ca snānena tālasyālepanena ca
ekacchattrapradānāc ca prāptā me suvarṇavarṇatā.
body.translated_text:
'By bathing in the bathhouse, by anointing with sandalwood paste,
and by offering a single umbrella, I obtained a golden complexion.'

body.text: evamādi chattrapradānasya vipāko vaktavyaḥ. āha ca.
body.translated_text: Thus the ripening of offering an umbrella should be described. And it says:

body.text: [notes only]
body.translated_text: [editorial notes]

body.text:
yad dhāryate pravaradaṇḍam udārarūpaṃ
kodaṇḍadāmaparimaṇḍitavastikośam
chattraṃ viśālam amalaṃ śaśimaṇḍalābham
chattrapradānajanitena jagaddharasya.
śrīcihnabhūtaṃ maṇihemadaṇḍam
paṭojjvalaṃ kāñcanam ātapatram
yad dhāryate mūrdhni narādhipasya
chattrapradānena jagaddharasya
body.translated_text:
'That which is held — an excellent staff of noble form,
with a covering-sheath adorned with bow-strings and cords,
an umbrella broad, spotless, resembling the moon's orb —
through the offering of an umbrella to the Lord of the World.
A jeweled golden-handled sunshade, bright with cloth,
the golden parasol, mark of <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity),
that which is held upon the head of the king of men —
through the offering of an umbrella to the Lord of the World.'

body.text: ime daśānuśaṃsaś chattrapradānasya.
body.translated_text: These are the ten benefits of offering an umbrella.

body.text: LXV. katame daśānuśaṃsā ghaṇṭāpradānasya. ucyate. abhirūpo bhavati. susvaro bhavati. manojñabhāṣī bhavati. kalaviṅkarutabhāṣī bhavati. ādeyavākyo bhavati. nityaṃ saṃprahāryajāto bhavati. punaḥ punar ānandaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti. svargeṣūpapadyate. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXV. What are the ten benefits of offering a bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>)? It is said: one becomes beautiful; one becomes sweet-voiced; one speaks pleasantly; one speaks like a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird; one's words carry weight; one is always filled with joy; again and again one hears joyful sounds; one is reborn in the heavens; one becomes of great wealth; and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) yathā viśākhayā mṛgāramātrā bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ. kathaṃ mama prāsāde nityaṃ kālaṃ pañcāṅgikaṃ tūryaṃ sadaiva vadet. bhagavān
body.translated_text: a) Just as <s>Viśākhā</s> <s>Mṛgāramātā</s> asked the Blessed One: 'How may the sound of a five-part orchestra always resound in my mansion?' The Blessed One

body.text: āha. sarvasvaropetāṃ ghaṇṭām āropaya. evaṃ te nityaṃ kālaṃ prāsāde pañcāṅgikatūryaśabdo bhaviṣyati. anavadyaś ca. ime daśa guṇā ghaṇṭāpradānasya.
body.translated_text: said: 'Set up a bell endowed with all tones. Thus in your mansion the sound of a five-part orchestra will always be heard. And it will be blameless.' These are the ten benefits of the gift of a bell.

body.text: LXVI. katame daśa guṇā vastrapradānasya. ucyate. ślakṣṇachavir bhavati. snigdhacchavir bhavati. na carajaś cailaṃ kāye śliṣyati. hrīrapatrāpyasaṃpanno bhavati priyadarśano bhavati prabhūtavastro bhavati lābhī ca bhavati sūkṣmāṇāṃ vastrāṇām āstaraṇānām. mahābhogo bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti. yathoktaṃ bhagavatā devatāsūtre. vastraprado bhavati varṇavān. ime daśa guṇānuśaṃsā vastrapradānasya.
body.translated_text: LXVI. What are the ten benefits of giving cloth? It is said: one has smooth skin, one has lustrous skin, dirt and grime do not cling to the body, one is endowed with modesty and shame, one is pleasant to look upon, one has abundant garments, one obtains fine and delicate fabrics and coverings, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. As the Blessed One said in the <s>Devatā Sūtra</s>: 'A giver of cloth becomes beautiful in complexion.' These are the ten benefits and advantages of giving cloth.

body.text: LXVII. katame daśānuśaṃsā āsanapradānasya. ucyate. gurusthānīyo bhavati lokasya. priyadarśano bhavati. prāsādiko bhavati. paṇḍitajanābhigamyo bhavati. yaśaḥ kīrtiś cāsya loke prathitā bhavati. sukhasaumanasyabahulo bhavati. svadeśe 'bhiramati. āsanair avaikalyaṃ bhavati. upasthāyakair avaikalyaṃ bhavati. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti. ime daśa guṇā āsanapradānasya.
body.translated_text: LXVII. What are the ten benefits of giving a seat? It is said: one becomes worthy of respect in the world, one is pleasant to look upon, one is serene, one is approached by the learned, one's fame and renown become celebrated in the world, one has abundant happiness and well-being, one delights in one's own country, there is no lack of seats, there is no lack of attendants, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. These are the ten benefits of giving a seat.

body.text: LXVIII. katame daśānuśaṃsā bhājanapradānasya. ucyate. bhājanabhūto bhavati guṇānāṃ snigdhasaṃtatir bhavati. na ca tṛṣābahulo bhavati. tṛṣārtasya pānīyaṃ prādurbhavati. na ca preteṣūpapadyate. bhājanair avaikalyaṃ bhavati. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti. ime daśānuśaṃsā bhājanapradānasya.
body.translated_text: LXVIII. What are the ten benefits of giving a vessel? It is said: one becomes a vessel of virtues, one has a smooth disposition, one is not excessively thirsty, water appears for the thirsty, one is not reborn among <s>preta</s>s (hungry ghosts), there is no lack of vessels, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. These are the ten benefits of giving a vessel.

body.text:
LXIX. katame daśānuśaṃsā bhojanapradānasya. ucyate. balavān bhavati. varṇavān bhavati. sukhito bhavati. pratibhānavān bhavati. dīrghāyur bhavati. mahājanābhigamyo bhavati. priyadarśano bhavati. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
a) yathoktaṃ bhagavatā vaiśālyāṃ siṃhasya rājaputrasya. dadan siṃha priyo bhavati. santo janā bhajanti. kalyāṇaśabdo bhavati. viśāradaḥ parṣadam avagāhati. kālagato deveṣūpapadyate.
gāthā coktā.
body.translated_text:
LXIX. What are the ten benefits of giving food? It is said: one becomes strong, one has fine complexion, one is happy, one has ready wit, one has a long life, one is approached by great multitudes, one is pleasant to look upon, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.
a) As the Blessed One said at <s>Vaiśālī</s> to Prince <s>Siṃha</s>: 'By giving, <s>Siṃha</s>, one becomes dear. The virtuous embrace one. One gains a good reputation. One enters an assembly with confidence. Having died, one is reborn among the gods.'
And a verse was spoken:

body.text:
te tatra nandanti ramanti ca modayanti
samarpitāḥ kāmaguṇeṣu pañcasu
kṛtvā hi vākyam amitasya tāyino
modanti te sugatavarasya śrāvakāḥ.
body.translated_text: They delight, rejoice, and exult there, furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure. Having followed the word of the Boundless Protector, the disciples of the Best of Well-Gone Ones rejoice.

body.text: etad dānasya phalaṃ bhagavatoktam.
body.translated_text: This is the fruit of giving as spoken by the Blessed One.

body.text: svargeṣūpapadyate kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti. āha ca.
body.translated_text: One is reborn in the heavens and quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And he said:

body.text:
nānārasavyañjanasupraṇītaṃ
kāle śubhaṃ gandharasopapannam
dadāti yaḥ pātram avekṣya dānaṃ
sadāryasaṃghasya guṇān vicintya
āyuś ca varṇaṃ ca yaśo balaṃ ca
saṃprāpya bhogān pratibhāṃ sukhaṃ ca
divīha caiva prathitottamaśrīḥ
sukhāt sukhaṃ yāti vimokṣam ante.
body.translated_text: He who gives food that is well-prepared with various flavors and seasonings, timely, auspicious, endowed with fragrance and taste, having regard for the worthy recipient, always reflecting on the virtues of the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> — having obtained long life, fine complexion, fame, strength, wealth, ready wit, and happiness, celebrated in the highest glory both here and in heaven, from happiness to happiness he goes, and to liberation in the end.

body.text: ime daśa guṇā bhojanapradānasya.
body.translated_text: These are the ten benefits of giving food.

body.text: LXX. katame daśa guṇā yānapradānasya. ucyate. sukumāracaraṇo bhavati. snpratiṣṭhitacaraṇo bhavati. mārgaklamatho na bhavati. na ca bahvamitro bhavati. punaḥ punaḥ ṛddhipādān pratilabhate. hastyaśvādibhir yānair avaikalyaṃ bhavati. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXX. What are the ten benefits of giving a vehicle? It is said: one has tender feet, one has well-placed feet, one does not suffer weariness on the road, one does not lack companions, one again and again attains the bases of supernatural power, there is no lack of vehicles such as elephants, horses, and the like, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) yathā coktaṃ devatāsūtre. yānadaḥ sukhito bhavati. yo dadāty upānahau. yathā coktam abhidharme cakravartisūtre. katamasya karmaṇo vipākena rājā cakravartī hastyaśvādīni vāhanāni pratilabhate. dīrgharātraṃ rājā cakravartī mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vopādhyāyaṃ vā skandhena vahati vā vāhayati vā. hastyaśvādibhiḥ śivikāyānair vā vahati vā. durgasaṃkramaṃ vā karoti. setubandhaṃ karoti. upānahapradānāni vā dadāti. kāruṇyena mahāṭavyāṃ sārtham atikrāmayati. tasya karmaṇo vipākena rājā cakravartī hastyaśvādīni pratilabhate. tatrārūḍhaḥ samudraparyantāṃ pṛthivīṃ divasacaturbhāgena paryaṭati. ime daśa guṇā yānapradānasya.
body.translated_text: a) As it is said in the <s>Devatā Sūtra</s>: 'A giver of vehicles becomes happy.' And the giver of sandals likewise. As it is said in the <s>Abhidharma Cakravartin Sūtra</s>: 'By the ripening of what <s>karma</s> does a <s>Cakravartin</s> king obtain vehicles such as elephants and horses? For a long time the <s>Cakravartin</s> king carries or causes to be carried on his shoulders his mother, father, or teacher. He conveys them by elephants, horses, palanquins, and vehicles. He builds crossings over difficult passages. He builds bridges. He gives gifts of sandals. Out of compassion he leads caravans across great forests. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, the <s>Cakravartin</s> king obtains elephants, horses, and the like. Mounted upon them, he traverses the earth bounded by the ocean in a quarter of a day.' These are the ten benefits
