body.text: LXXI. katame daśa guṇāḥ pratiśrayapradānasya. ucyate. rājā bhavati prādeśikaḥ. rājā bhavati māṇḍalikaḥ. rājā bhavati jambudvīpādhipatiḥ. rājā bhavati dvīpadvayādhipatiḥ. rājā bhavati dvīpatrayādhipatiḥ. rājā bhavati caturdvīpādhipatiś cakravartī. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXXI. What are the ten benefits of giving shelter? It is said: one becomes a provincial king, one becomes a regional king, one becomes lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, one becomes lord of two continents, one becomes lord of three continents, one becomes a <s>Cakravartin</s> king ruling four continents, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: yathā sumedhāyā bhikṣuṇyā gāthā.
body.translated_text: As in the verses of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Sumedhā</s>:

body.text:
bhagavati konāgamunau saṃghārāme ca niveśe
sakhyas trayo vayaṃ sa vihāraṃ dadau pūrvam.
body.translated_text: When the Blessed <s>Konāgamuni</s> was present, we three friends — she gave a monastery to the <s>Saṃgha</s> first.

body.text: etā gāthā sumedhāyāḥ. dharmadinnā ca bhikṣuṇī viśākhyā ca mṛgāramātā. tābhiḥ pūrvaṃ daridrastrībhiś catvāri kāṣṭhāni nikhanya kāśakaṭakam upari dattvā bhagavān konāgamunir buddho nimantritaḥ. sa tatra bhikṣubhiḥ sārdhaṃ muhūrtaṃ viśrāntaḥ. tābhiś cittāni prasāditāni. tena karmaṇā śatasahasraṃ vārān deveṣūpapannāḥ. aparimitāni cakravartirāṣṭrāny anubhūtāni. sumedhāgāthāś cāsminn arthe sarvā vistareṇa pratyekam avagantavyāḥ. ime daśa guṇāḥ pratiśrayapradānasya.
body.translated_text: These are the verses of <s>Sumedhā</s>. And the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Dharmadinnā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s> <s>Mṛgāramātā</s>. Formerly, when they were poor women, they planted four stakes and placed a reed hut on top, and invited the Blessed <s>Konāgamuni</s> Buddha. He rested there for a moment with the monks. They generated faith in their minds. By that <s>karma</s>, they were reborn among the gods a hundred thousand times. They experienced immeasurable kingdoms as <s>Cakravartin</s>s. The verses of <s>Sumedhā</s> should all be understood in detail, each individually, in this context. These are the ten benefits of giving shelter.

body.text: LXXII. katame daśa guṇāḥ pānakapradānasya. ucyate. sarvendriyasaṃpanno bhavati. prasannavadano. viśuddhalalāṭaḥ. snigdhacchaviḥ. saṃgatabhāṣī bhavati. na ca tṛṣābahulo bhavati. tṛṣitasya
body.translated_text: LXXII. What are the ten benefits of giving drink? It is said: one is endowed with all sense faculties, one has a serene countenance, one has a clear forehead, one has lustrous skin, one speaks agreeably, one is not excessively thirsty, for the thirsty

body.text: pānīyaṃ prādurbhavati. na ca preteṣūpapadyate. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti. yathā cāha.
body.translated_text: water appears, one is not reborn among <s>preta</s>s (hungry ghosts), one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And it is said:

body.text:
manojñavarṇaṃ rasagandhayuktaṃ
sarvendriyaprītivivardhanaṃ ca
akālikaṃ satpuruṣapraśastaṃ
dadāti saṃghāya tu pānakaṃ yaḥ
sakṛtpipāsāvigato viśoko
rasān pradhānāñ caturo 'nubhūya
jagac ca saddharmarasena tarpya
tṛṣākṣayaṃ yāti sukhaṃ sukhena.
body.translated_text: He who gives to the <s>Saṃgha</s> a drink that is delightful in color, endowed with flavor and fragrance, increasing the joy of all the senses, timely and praised by the virtuous — once freed from thirst and sorrow, having experienced the four chief flavors, and having satisfied the world with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>, he goes happily from happiness to the exhaustion of craving.

body.text: ime daśa guṇāḥ pānakapradānasya.
body.translated_text: These are the ten benefits of giving drink.

body.text: LXXIII. katame daśa guṇā mālāpradānasya. ucyate. mālābhūto bhavati lokasya. kāyād daurgandhyam apaiti saugandhyaṃ prādurbhavati. nityasugandho nityālaṃkṛto bhavati. abhedyaparivāro bhavati. sarvajanapriyo bhavati. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXXIII. What are the ten benefits of giving garlands? It is said: one becomes a garland to the world, bodily foul odor departs and fragrance appears, one is always fragrant, one is always adorned, one has an unbreakable retinue, one is dear to all people, one has great wealth, one is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) aha ca.
body.translated_text: a) And it is said:

body.text:
mālyaṃ vicitraṃ pravaraṃ sugandhaṃ
praharṣaṇaṃ prītikaraṃ narāṇām
prasannacitto munidhātugarbhe
tathāgatebhyaś ca dadāti yo vai
sa divyamālyābharaṇojjvalāṅgaḥ
śrīmat sukhaṃ prāpya divīha caiva
bodhyaṅgadāmapratibhūṣitātmā
mokṣaṃ paraṃ yāti guṇāgragandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: He who, with a serene mind, gives to the <s>Tathāgata</s>s and to the reliquary shrines of the sage various, excellent, fragrant garlands that delight and please people — his body radiant with divine garlands and ornaments, having obtained glorious happiness both here and in heaven, his self adorned with the garland of the factors of awakening, he goes to the supreme liberation, foremost in the fragrance of virtues.

body.text: b) tathānyatarasya daridragṛhapater duhitā. sā khalu dvāre sthitā janapadaṃ sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitaṃ paśyati. utsave ramamāṇam. sā pitaram āha. mām apy alaṃkuruṣveti. pitāha. kuto 'smākaṃ daridrāṇām alaṃkāraḥ. eṣa janapadaḥ kṛtapuṇyo 'nekaśo buddhe bhagavati kṛtādhikāraḥ. tena ca karmaṇā karṇesumanasya sthavirasyāvadānaṃ vistaraśas tasyoktam. evam alpo 'pi bhagavati kṛtaḥ prasādo mahāphalo bhavati. tayā pitātīvoparodhitaḥ prayaccha mama kiṃcid eṣo 'grato vihāraḥ atra bhagavataḥ pūjām upariṣyāmīti. tena duḥkhārtena vibhave 'vidyamāne palālamayīṃ mālāṃ kṛtvā dattā. sā tāṃ palālamayīṃ mālāṃ gṛhya buddhapratimāyāḥ śirasi dattvā pādayoḥ praṇipatya āha. bhagavann anena kuśalamūlena saṃsāre saṃsaratyā mā bhūyaḥ dāridryaṃ syād iti. tasyāḥ prasādajātāyās tad ahar eva mānuṣyaṃ strībhāvam atikrāntaṃ divyaṃ rūpaṃ prādurbhūtam. tadviṣayaprativāsinā ca rājñāgradevī sthāpitā. kālagatā deveṣūpapannā. paścime 'pi ca bhave campāyām agrakulikasya
body.translated_text: b) Likewise, the daughter of a certain poor householder. She, standing at the door, saw the entire countryside adorned with all ornaments, delighting in a festival. She said to her father: 'Adorn me too.' The father said: 'Where would we poor people get ornaments? This countryside has made merit, having performed meritorious deeds many times toward the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>.' And by that <s>karma</s>, the story of the elder <s>Karṇesumanas</s> was told to her in detail. 'Thus even a small act of faith performed toward the Blessed One bears great fruit.' She pressured her father greatly: 'Give me something — this monastery is right in front; I shall make an offering to the Blessed One there.' He, distressed by poverty and having no resources, made a garland of straw and gave it to her. She, taking that straw garland, placed it on the head of the <s>Buddha</s> image, bowed at his feet, and said: 'Blessed One, by this root of merit, as I wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>, may I never again have poverty.' For her, who had generated faith, on that very day her human female form was transcended and a divine form appeared. And the king of that region made her his chief queen. Having died, she was reborn among the gods. And even in her final birth, in <s>Campā</s>, as the daughter of a chief family

body.text: duhitā pratyājātā paramakalyāṇī sauvarṇā cāsyā mālā sarvaratnamaṇḍitā śirasi sahasaiva prādurbhūtā. mātāpitṛbhyāṃ vismayajātābhyāṃ mālinīty evāsyā nāma kṛtam. yadā ca bhagavān abhisaṃbuddho rājagṛhāc campām anuprāptaḥ. sā copasaṃkrāntā. tasyāś ca bhagavatā dharmadeśanā kṛtā pravrajitā cārhantī saṃvṛttā. sāha cittotpādād evāsyā mā me bhūyo mālā bhavatv ity antarhitā. tāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vismayaprāptā devatā gāthām anugāyate yathāha.
body.translated_text: she was reborn, supremely beautiful, and a golden garland adorned with all kinds of gems suddenly appeared on her head. Her parents, filled with wonder, gave her the name <s>Mālinī</s> ('Garland-bearer'). And when the Blessed One, having attained full enlightenment, arrived at <s>Campā</s> from <s>Rājagṛha</s>, she approached him. The Blessed One taught her the <s>Dharma</s>, and she went forth and became an <s>Arhatī</s>. She said, 'By the arising of this thought, may I no longer have this garland' — and it vanished. And a deity, having seen that and being struck with wonder, sang a verse as follows:

body.text:
dattvā tu palālamayīṃ mālāṃ sā mālinī sugatasya caitye
varakanakaratnamālāṃ lebhe bodhyaṅgamālāṃ ca.
body.translated_text:
Having given a straw garland to the shrine of the <s>Sugata</s>,
that <s>Mālinī</s> obtained a garland of the finest gold and gems, and the garland of the factors of awakening.

body.text: ime daśa guṇā mālāpradānasya.
body.translated_text: These are the ten benefits of giving garlands.

body.text: LXXIV. katame daśa guṇā muktapuṣpapradānasya. ucyate. puṣpabhūto bhavati lokasya. ghrāṇendriyaṃ viśudhyati. kāyadaurgandhyaṃ samapaiti. saugandhyaṃ prādurbhavati. daśa diśaḥ śīlagandhaḥ khyātiṃ gacchati. abhigamanīyaś ca bhavati. lābhī ca bhavati
body.translated_text: LXXIV. What are the ten benefits of giving loose flowers? It is said: one becomes like a flower to the world. The sense of smell becomes purified. Bodily foul odor departs. Fragrance appears. The fragrance of one's virtue (<s>śīla</s>) becomes renowned in the ten directions. One becomes approachable. One becomes a recipient

body.text: iṣṭānāṃ dharmāṇām. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: of desirable qualities. One becomes wealthy. One is reborn in the heavens, and one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) atra karṇesumanasya pūrvajanmani prasāde jāte ekaikapuṣpapradānasya vipāko vaktavyaḥ. yathā sa eva āha.
body.translated_text: a) Here the ripening of the offering of a single flower by <s>Karṇesumanas</s> in a previous birth, when faith had arisen, should be told. As he himself said:

body.text:
ekapuṣpapradānena aśītikalpakoṭayaḥ
durgatiṃ nābhijānāmi buddhapūjāya tat phalam.
body.translated_text:
By the giving of a single flower, for eighty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s>
I have not known a bad rebirth — that is the fruit of worshipping the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: ime daśa guṇā muktapuṣpapradānasya.
body.translated_text: These are the ten benefits of giving loose flowers.

body.text: LXXV. katame daśa guṇā dīpapradānasya. ucyate. pradīpabhūto bhavati lokasya. māṃsacakṣur naśyati. divyacakṣuḥ prādurbhavati. avidyāndhakāraṃ vidhamati. jñānāloka utpadyate. kuśalākuśalān dharmān kṣipraṃ prajñayā pratividhyati. saṃsāre saṃsarato 'vidyāndhakāro na bhavati. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXXV. What are the ten benefits of giving lamps? It is said: one becomes a lamp to the world. The fleshly eye passes away and the divine eye appears. One dispels the darkness of ignorance. The light of knowledge arises. One quickly penetrates with wisdom the distinction between wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. While wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the darkness of ignorance does not exist. One becomes wealthy. One is reborn in the heavens. And one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) yathā coktam abhidharme cakravartisūtravibhaṅge. kasya karmaṇo vipākena rājā cakravartī maṇiratnaṃ pratilabhate. dīrgharātraṃ rājñā cakravartinā dīpapradānāni pradattāni. pradīpaikadānāni ca. andhakāre ratnapradīpā dhāritā. ye cakṣuṣmantas te samaviṣamāṇi rūpāṇi paśyantu. āha ca.
body.translated_text: a) As stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, in the <s>Cakravartisūtravibhaṅga</s>: 'By the ripening of what <s>karma</s> does the <s>Cakravartin</s> king obtain the jewel-treasure?' The <s>Cakravartin</s> king gave lamp-offerings for a long time. And he gave individual lamp-gifts. In the darkness he held gem-lamps, [saying]: 'Let those who have eyes see both beautiful and ugly forms.' And it is said:

body.text:
buddhapraśastaṃ labhate ca cakṣuś
cakṣus tu yasyottamahetubhūtam
lokāvabhāsaṃ bhavatīha rūpam
pradīpadānena jagaddharasya.
tejo'dhiko nārtham udīkṣaṇīyaḥ
atīva tuṣṭaḥ śubhakarmadarśī
saṃprāpya saukhyaṃ divi ceha caiva
viśuddhacakṣuḥ praśamaṃ paraiti.
body.translated_text:
One obtains the eye praised by the <s>Buddha</s>,
and the eye that is the supreme cause —
the form that illuminates the world arises here
from giving lamps to the Lord of the World.
Abounding in splendor, not to be looked upon,
exceedingly pleased, seeing his own good <s>karma</s>,
having attained happiness both in heaven and here,
with purified vision he goes to final peace.

body.text: atrāryāniruddhasya dīpe divyacakṣur ṛṣīṇāṃ ca cakṣūtpāṭanamokṣāyaṇe vaktavyam. yathā dīpamālāpradānena dīpaṅkareṇa buddhatvaṃ prāptam. yā ca śrāvastyāṃ cakṣuvikalena pradīpamālā kāritā. saprasādo jātaḥ. praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān. utthitasya cāsya yathā paurāṇaṃ cakṣuḥ saṃvṛttam. ime daśa guṇā dīpapradānasya.
body.translated_text: Here the story of the noble <s>Aniruddha</s>'s divine eye through a lamp, and the story of the deliverance of the <s>ṛṣis</s> whose eyes had been plucked out, should be told. Just as through the offering of rows of lamps, <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> attained Buddhahood. And just as in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a blind person had a row of lamps made, and faith was born in him, and he made a vow. And when he arose, his eyes became as they were before. These are the ten benefits of giving lamps.

body.text: LXXVI. katame daśa guṇā gandhapradānasya. ucyate. gandhabhūto bhavati lokasya. ghrāṇendriyaṃ viśudhyati. kāyadaurgandhyam apaiti. saugandhyaṃ prādurbhavati. daśa diśaḥ śīlagandhaḥ pravāti. abhigamanīyo bhavati. lābhī ca bhavati iṣṭānāṃ dharmāṇām. mahābhogaś ca bhavati. svargeṣūpapadyate. kṣipraṃ ca parinirvāti.
body.translated_text: LXXVI. What are the ten benefits of giving incense? It is said: one becomes like incense to the world. The sense of smell becomes purified. Bodily foul odor departs. Fragrance appears. The fragrance of one's virtue blows in the ten directions. One becomes approachable. One becomes a recipient of desirable qualities. One becomes wealthy. One is reborn in the heavens. And one quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: a) yathoktam abhidharme cakravartisūtre. kasya karmaṇo vipākena rājñaś cakravartinaḥ strīratnasya romakūpebhyaḥ śarīrād gandho nirgacchati. tadyathā gandhasamudgakasya. dīrgharātraṃ tayā striyā caityagarbhagṛheṣu gandhopalepanāni dattāni. surabhīṇi ca puṣpāṇi dhūpaś ca dattāḥ. stūpeṣu ca gandhasnāpanāni kṛtāni. tasya karmaṇo vipākena rājñaś cakravartinaḥ strīratnasya śarīrād evaṃrūpo gandho nirgacchati. tadyathā gandhakaraṇḍasya. ime daśa guṇā gandhapradānasya.
body.translated_text: a) As stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, in the <s>Cakravartisūtra</s>: 'By the ripening of what <s>karma</s> does fragrance emanate from the pores and body of the <s>Cakravartin</s> king's jewel-woman, as if from a casket of incense?' That woman, for a long time, gave incense-anointings in the inner chambers of <s>caityas</s> (shrines), and offered fragrant flowers and incense. And she performed fragrant bathings at <s>stūpas</s>. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, such fragrance emanates from the body of the <s>Cakravartin</s> king's jewel-woman, as if from a basket of incense. These are the ten benefits of giving incense.

body.text: LXXVII. katame daśa guṇāḥ pravrajyāyāḥ. ucyate. putrabhāryaduhitṛdhanatṛṣṇāsya na bhavati. kāmasya parigraho na bhavati. araṇyavāse prītiṃ pratilabhate. buddhagocaraṃ sevate. bālagocaraṃ vivarjayati. durgatigamanīyān dharmān vivarjayati. sugatigamanīyān dharmān sevate. devā asya spṛhayanti. nityaṃ sugatavacane pravrajyāṃ pratilabhate. ime daśa guṇāḥ pravrajyāyā bhavanti.
body.translated_text: LXXVII. What are the ten benefits of going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>)? It is said: one has no craving for sons, wife, daughters, or wealth. One has no attachment to sense pleasures. One obtains delight in forest dwelling. One frequents the domain of <s>Buddhas</s>. One avoids the domain of fools. One avoids <s>dharmas</s> that lead to bad destinations. One practices <s>dharmas</s> that lead to good destinations. The gods envy one. One constantly obtains ordination into the <s>Sugata</s>'s teaching. These are the ten benefits of going forth.

body.text: LXXVIII. katame daśa guṇā araṇyavāsasya. ucyate. saṃgaṇikā vivarjayati. pravivekaṃ sevate. dhyānālambanaṃ cittaṃ bhavati. na ca bahukarmakṛtyatāṃ prāpnoti. buddhānāṃ smṛtiṃ yāti. prītisukhasaumanasyaṃ kāyo na jahāti. antarāyāś ca na bhavanti. brahmacaryasya alpāyāsena samādhim adhigacchati. uddiṣṭaṃ cāsya padavyañjanaṃ na naśyati. yathāśrutānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vistareṇārtham ājānati. ime daśa guṇā araṇyavāsasya.
body.translated_text: LXXVIII. What are the ten benefits of forest dwelling? It is said: one avoids socializing. One cultivates seclusion. The mind becomes focused on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). One does not become burdened with many tasks and duties. One comes into the remembrance of <s>Buddhas</s>. Joy, happiness, and well-being do not leave the body. Hindrances do not arise. One attains <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) with little effort in the holy life. What has been taught to one — the words and syllables — do not perish. One understands in detail the meaning of the <s>dharmas</s> one has heard. These are the ten benefits of forest dwelling.

body.text: LXXIX. katame daśa guṇāḥ paiṇḍapātikatve. ucyate. caṅkramo 'sya upārjito bhavati. gocaro 'sya prahato bhavati. māno 'sya nihato
body.translated_text: LXXIX. What are the ten benefits of the practice of alms-begging (<s>paiṇḍapātika</s>)? It is said: one's walking meditation is well-practiced. One's alms-round is accomplished. One's pride is struck down

body.text: bhavati. ātmānaṃ lābhena yojayati. parān puṇye pratiṣṭhāpayati. śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ dīpayati. paścimāyā janatāyā ālokaḥ kṛto bhavati. sabrahmacāriṇām upaghātaḥ kṛto na bhavati. nīcacittam upasthāpitaṃ bhavati. piṇḍapātaparacittasya bhikṣoḥ sarvā diśo 'pratikūlā bhavanti gamanāya. ime daśa guṇāḥ piṇḍapātikatve.
body.translated_text: One applies oneself to gain. One establishes others in merit. One illuminates the Teacher's teaching. One becomes a light for future generations. One does not cause harm to fellow practitioners of the holy life. One maintains a humble mind. For a <s>bhikṣu</s> whose mind is set on alms-food, all directions are favorable for going. These are the ten benefits of the practice of alms-begging.

body.text: LXXX. daśa vaiśāradyāni. katamāni daśa. ucyate. viśārado grāmaṃ praviśati. viśārado grāmān niṣkrāmati. viśāradaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte. viśāradaḥ pariṣadi dharmaṃ deśayati. viśāradaḥ saṃghamadhyam avatarati. viśārada ācāryopādhyāyān upasaṃkrāmati. viśārado maitracittaḥ śiṣyān anuśāsti. viśāradaś cīvarapiiiḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān paribhuṅkte. grāhyaṃ cāsya vaco bhavati. imāni daśa vaiśāradyāni.
body.translated_text: LXXX. Ten forms of self-confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). What are the ten? It is said: with self-confidence one enters the village. With self-confidence one departs from the village. With self-confidence one partakes of alms-food. With self-confidence one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in an assembly. With self-confidence one enters the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. With self-confidence one approaches teachers and preceptors. With self-confidence and a mind of loving-kindness one instructs disciples. With self-confidence one makes use of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick. And one's word is to be heeded. These are the ten forms of self-confidence.

body.text: karmavibhaṅgasūtraṃ samāptam
body.translated_text: The <s>Karmavibhaṅga Sūtra</s> is concluded.
